docs.title: Event Priorities
docs.text:
For each event type, corresponding methods of plugins are called in the order that the plugins appear in the plugins config.

Since MkDocs 1.4, plugins can choose to set a priority value for their events. Events with higher priority are called first. Events without a chosen priority get a default of 0. Events that have the same priority are ordered as they appear in the config.

docs.title: Handling Errors
docs.text: MkDocs defines four error types:

docs.title: ::: mkdocs.exceptions.PluginError
docs.text:
Unexpected and uncaught exceptions will interrupt the build process and produce typical Python tracebacks, which are useful for debugging your code. However, users generally find tracebacks overwhelming and often miss the helpful error message. Therefore, MkDocs will catch any of the errors listed above, retrieve the error message, and exit immediately with only the helpful message displayed to the user.

Therefore, you might want to catch any exceptions within your plugin and raise a PluginError, passing in your own custom-crafted message, so that the build process is aborted with a helpful message.

The on_build_error event will be triggered for any exception.

For example:

from mkdocs.exceptions import PluginError
from mkdocs.plugins import BasePlugin


class MyPlugin(BasePlugin):
    def on_post_page(self, output, page, config, **kwargs):
        try:
            # some code that could throw a KeyError
            ...
        except KeyError as error:
            raise PluginError(str(error))

    def on_build_error(self, error, **kwargs):
        # some code to clean things up
        ...

docs.title: Entry Point
docs.text:
Plugins need to be packaged as Python libraries (distributed on PyPI separate from MkDocs) and each must register as a Plugin via a setuptools entry_points. Add the following to your setup.py script:

entry_points={
    'mkdocs.plugins': [
        'pluginname = path.to.some_plugin:SomePluginClass',
    ]
}

The pluginname would be the name used by users (in the config file) and path.to.some_plugin:SomePluginClass would be the importable plugin itself (from path.to.some_plugin import SomePluginClass) where SomePluginClass is a subclass of BasePlugin which defines the plugin behavior. Naturally, multiple Plugin classes could exist in the same module. Simply define each as a separate entry point.

entry_points={
    'mkdocs.plugins': [
        'featureA = path.to.my_plugins:PluginA',
        'featureB = path.to.my_plugins:PluginB'
    ]
}

Note that registering a plugin does not activate it. The user still needs to tell MkDocs to use it via the config.

docs.title: Developing Themes
docs.text:
A guide to creating and distributing custom themes.

NOTE: If you are looking for existing third party themes, they are listed in the community wiki page and Best-of-MkDocs. If you want to share a theme you create, you should list it there.

When creating a new theme, you can either follow the steps in this guide to create one from scratch or you can download the mkdocs-basic-theme as a basic, yet complete, theme with all the boilerplate required. You can find this base theme on GitHub. It contains detailed comments in the code to describe the different features and their usage.

docs.title: Creating a custom theme
docs.text:
The bare minimum required for a custom theme is a main.html Jinja2 template file which is placed in a directory that is not a child of the docs_dir. Within mkdocs.yml, set the theme.custom_dir option to the path of the directory containing main.html. The path should be relative to the configuration file. For example, given this example project layout:

mkdocs.yml
docs/
    index.md
    about.md
custom_theme/
    main.html
    ...

... you would include the following settings in mkdocs.yml to use the custom theme directory:

theme:
    name: null
    custom_dir: 'custom_theme/'

NOTE: Generally, when building your own custom theme, the theme.name configuration setting would be set to null. However, if the theme.custom_dir configuration value is used in combination with an existing theme, the theme.custom_dir can be used to replace only specific parts of a built-in theme. For example, with the above layout and if you set name: "mkdocs" then the main.html file in the theme.custom_dir would replace the file of the same name in the mkdocs theme but otherwise the mkdocs theme would remain unchanged. This is useful if you want to make small adjustments to an existing theme.

For more specific information, see Customizing Your Theme.

WARNING: A theme's configuration defined in a mkdocs_theme.yml file is not loaded from theme.custom_dir. When an entire theme exists in theme.custom_dir and theme.name is set to null, then the entire theme configuration must be defined in the theme configuration option in the mkdocs.yml file.

However, when a theme is packaged up for distribution, and loaded using the theme.name configuration option, then a mkdocs_theme.yml file is required for the theme.

docs.title: Basic theme
docs.text:
The simplest main.html file is the following:

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <title>{% if page.title %}{{ page.title }} - {% endif %}{{ config.site_name }}</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    {{ page.content }}
  </body>
</html>

The body content from each page specified in mkdocs.yml is inserted using the {{ page.content }} tag. Style-sheets and scripts can be brought into this theme as with a normal HTML file. Navbars and tables of contents can also be generated and included automatically, through the nav and toc objects, respectively. If you wish to write your own theme, it is recommended to start with one of the built-in themes and modify it accordingly.

NOTE: As MkDocs uses Jinja as its template engine, you have access to all the power of Jinja, including template inheritance. You may notice that the themes included with MkDocs make extensive use of template inheritance and blocks, allowing users to easily override small bits and pieces of the templates from the theme custom_dir. Therefore, the built-in themes are implemented in a base.html file, which main.html extends. Although not required, third party template authors are encouraged to follow a similar pattern and may want to define the same blocks as are used in the built-in themes for consistency.

docs.title: Theme Files
docs.text: There are various files which a theme treats special in some way. Any other files are simply copied from the theme directory to the same path in the site_dir when the site it built. For example image and CSS files have no special significance and are copied as-is. Note, however, that if the user provides a file with the same path in their docs_dir, then the user's file will replace the theme file.

docs.title: Template Files
docs.text: Any files with the .html extension are considered to be template files and are not copied from the theme directory or any subdirectories. Also, any files listed in static_templates are treated as templates regardless of their file extension.

docs.title: Theme Meta Files
docs.text: The various files required for packaging a theme are also ignored. Specifically, the mkdocs_theme.yml configuration file and any Python files.

docs.title: Dot Files
docs.text:
Theme authors can explicitly force MkDocs to ignore files by starting a file or directory name with a dot. Any of the following files would be ignored:

.ignored.txt
.ignored/file.txt
foo/.ignored.txt
foo/.ignored/file.txt

docs.title: Documentation Files
docs.text: All documentation files are ignored. Specifically, any Markdown files (using any of the file extensions supported by MKDocs). Additionally, any README files which may exist in the theme directories are ignored.

docs.title: Template Variables
docs.text: Each template in a theme is built with a template context. These are the variables that are available to themes. The context varies depending on the template that is being built. At the moment templates are either built with the global context or with a page specific context. The global context is used for HTML pages that don't represent an individual Markdown document, for example a 404.html page or search.html.

docs.title: Global Context
docs.text: The following variables are available globally on any template.

docs.title: config
docs.text:
The config variable is an instance of MkDocs' config object generated from the mkdocs.yml config file. While you can use any config option, some commonly used options include:

  • config.site_name
  • config.site_url
  • config.site_author
  • config.site_description
  • config.theme.locale (See also Theme Configuration below)
  • config.extra_javascript
  • config.extra_css
  • config.repo_url
  • config.repo_name
  • config.copyright
  • config.google_analytics

docs.title: nav
docs.text:
The nav variable is used to create the navigation for the documentation. The nav object is an iterable of navigation objects as defined by the nav configuration setting.

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Navigation options: show_root_heading: false show_root_toc_entry: true members: [] heading_level: 4

In addition to the iterable of navigation objects, the nav object contains the following attributes:

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Navigation.homepage options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Navigation.pages options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

This list is not necessarily a complete list of all site pages as it does not contain pages which are not included in the navigation. This list does match the list and order of pages used for all "next page" and "previous page" links. For a list of all pages, use the pages template variable.

docs.title: Nav Example
docs.text:
Following is a basic usage example which outputs the first and second level navigation as a nested list.

{% if nav|length>1 %}
    <ul>
    {% for nav_item in nav %}
        {% if nav_item.children %}
            <li>{{ nav_item.title }}
                <ul>
                {% for nav_item in nav_item.children %}
                    <li class="{% if nav_item.active %}current{% endif %}">
                        <a href="{{ nav_item.url|url }}">{{ nav_item.title }}</a>
                    </li>
                {% endfor %}
                </ul>
            </li>
        {% else %}
            <li class="{% if nav_item.active %}current{% endif %}">
                <a href="{{ nav_item.url|url }}">{{ nav_item.title }}</a>
            </li>
        {% endif %}
    {% endfor %}
    </ul>
{% endif %}

docs.title: base_url
docs.text: The base_url provides a relative path to the root of the MkDocs project. While this can be used directly by prepending it to a local relative URL, it is best to use the url template filter, which is smarter about how it applies base_url.

docs.title: mkdocs_version
docs.text: Contains the current MkDocs version.

docs.title: build_date_utc
docs.text: A Python datetime object that represents the date and time the documentation was built in UTC. This is useful for showing how recently the documentation was updated.

docs.title: pages
docs.text: A flat list of File objects for all pages in the project. This list can contain pages not included in the global navigation and may not match the order of pages within that navigation. The page object for each File can be accessed from file.page.

docs.title: page
docs.text:
In templates which are not rendered from a Markdown source file, the page variable is None. In templates which are rendered from a Markdown source file, the page variable contains a page object. The same page objects are used as page navigation objects in the global navigation and in the pages template variable.

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page options: show_root_heading: false show_root_toc_entry: true members: [] heading_level: 4

All page objects contain the following attributes:

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.title options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.content options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.toc options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

The following example would display the top two levels of the Table of Contents for a page.

<ul>
{% for toc_item in page.toc %}
    <li><a href="{{ toc_item.url }}">{{ toc_item.title }}</a></li>
    {% for toc_item in toc_item.children %}
        <li><a href="{{ toc_item.url }}">{{ toc_item.title }}</a></li>
    {% endfor %}
{% endfor %}
</ul>

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.meta options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

In this example we define a source property above the page title:

source: generics.py
        mixins.py

# Page title

Content...

A template can access this metadata for the page with the meta.source variable. This could then be used to link to source files related to the documentation page.

{% for filename in page.meta.source %}
  <a class="github" href="https://github.com/.../{{ filename }}">
    <span class="label label-info">{{ filename }}</span>
  </a>
{% endfor %}

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.url options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

It is expected that this be used with the url filter to ensure the URL is relative to the current page.

<a href="{{ page.url|url }}">{{ page.title }}</a>

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.file options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.abs_url options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

For example, if site_url: https://example.com/, then the value of page.abs_url for the page foo.md would be /foo/. However, if site_url: https://example.com/bar/, then the value of page.abs_url for the page foo.md would be /bar/foo/.

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.canonical_url options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.edit_url options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.is_homepage options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

This can be used in conjunction with other attributes of the page object to alter the behavior. For example, to display a different title on the homepage:

{% if not page.is_homepage %}{{ page.title }} - {% endif %}{{ site_name }}

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.previous_page options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.next_page options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.parent options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.children options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.active options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.is_section options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.is_page options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.pages.Page.is_link options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

docs.title: AnchorLink
docs.text: ::: mkdocs.structure.toc.AnchorLink options: show_root_heading: false show_root_toc_entry: true heading_level: 5

docs.title: Navigation Objects
docs.text:
Navigation objects contained in the nav template variable may be one of section objects, page objects, and link objects. While section objects may contain nested navigation objects, pages and links do not.

Page objects are the full page object as used for the current page with all of the same attributes available. Section and Link objects contain a subset of those attributes as defined below:

docs.title: Section
docs.text:
A section navigation object defines a named section in the navigation and contains a list of child navigation objects. Note that sections do not contain URLs and are not links of any kind. However, by default, MkDocs sorts index pages to the top and the first child might be used as the URL for a section if a theme chooses to do so.

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Section options: show_root_heading: false show_root_toc_entry: true members: [] heading_level: 4

The following attributes are available on section objects:

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Section.title options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Section.parent options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Section.children options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Section.active options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Section.is_section options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Section.is_page options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Section.is_link options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

docs.title: Link
docs.text:
A link navigation object contains a link which does not point to an internal MkDocs page.

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Link options: show_root_heading: false show_root_toc_entry: true members: [] heading_level: 4

The following attributes are available on link objects:

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Link.title options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Link.url options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Link.parent options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Link.children options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Link.active options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Link.is_section options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Link.is_page options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

::: mkdocs.structure.nav.Link.is_link options: show_root_full_path: false heading_level: 5

docs.title: Extra Context
docs.text:
Additional variables can be passed to the template with the extra configuration option. This is a set of key value pairs that can make custom templates far more flexible.

For example, this could be used to include the project version of all pages and a list of links related to the project. This can be achieved with the following extra configuration:

extra:
    version: 0.13.0
    links:
        - https://github.com/mkdocs
        - https://docs.readthedocs.org/en/latest/builds.html#mkdocs
        - https://www.mkdocs.org/

And then displayed with this HTML in the custom theme.

{{ config.extra.version }}

{% if config.extra.links %}
  <ul>
  {% for link in config.extra.links %}
      <li>{{ link }}</li>
  {% endfor %}
  </ul>
{% endif %}

docs.title: Template Filters
docs.text: In addition to Jinja's default filters, the following custom filters are available to use in MkDocs templates:

docs.title: url
docs.text:
Normalizes a URL. Absolute URLs are passed through unaltered. If the URL is relative and the template context includes a page object, then the URL is returned relative to the page object. Otherwise, the URL is returned with base_url prepended.

<a href="{{ page.url|url }}">{{ page.title }}</a>

docs.title: tojson
docs.text:
Safety convert a Python object to a value in a JavaScript script.

<script>
    var mkdocs_page_name = {{ page.title|tojson|safe }};
</script>

docs.title: Search and themes
docs.text:
As of MkDocs version 0.17 client side search support has been added to MkDocs via the search plugin. A theme needs to provide a few things for the plugin to work with the theme.

While the search plugin is activated by default, users can disable the plugin and themes should account for this. It is recommended that theme templates wrap search specific markup with a check for the plugin:

{% if 'search' in config['plugins'] %}
    search stuff here...
{% endif %}

At its most basic functionality, the search plugin will simply provide an index file which is no more than a JSON file containing the content of all pages. The theme would need to implement its own search functionality client-side. However, with a few settings and the necessary templates, the plugin can provide a complete functioning client-side search tool based on lunr.js.

The following HTML needs to be added to the theme so that the provided JavaScript is able to properly load the search scripts and make relative links to the search results from the current page.

<script>var base_url = '{{ base_url }}';</script>

With properly configured settings, the following HTML in a template will add a full search implementation to your theme.

<h1 id="search">Search Results</h1>

<form action="search.html">
  <input name="q" id="mkdocs-search-query" type="text" >
</form>

<div id="mkdocs-search-results">
  Sorry, page not found.
</div>

The JavaScript in the plugin works by looking for the specific ID's used in the above HTML. The form input for the user to type the search query must be identified with id="mkdocs-search-query" and the div where the results will be placed must be identified with id="mkdocs-search-results".

The plugin supports the following options being set in the theme's configuration file, mkdocs_theme.yml:

docs.title: include_search_page
docs.text:
Determines whether the search plugin expects the theme to provide a dedicated search page via a template located at search/search.html.

When include_search_page is set to true, the search template will be built and available at search/search.html. This method is used by the readthedocs theme.

When include_search_page is set to false or not defined, it is expected that the theme provide some other mechanisms for displaying search results. For example, the mkdocs theme displays results on any page via a modal.

docs.title: search_index_only
docs.text:
Determines whether the search plugin should only generate a search index or a complete search solution.

When search_index_only is set to false, then the search plugin modifies the Jinja environment by adding its own templates directory (with a lower precedence than the theme) and adds its scripts to the extra_javascript config setting.

When search_index_only is set to true or not defined, the search plugin makes no modifications to the Jinja environment. A complete solution using the provided index file is the responsibility of the theme.

The search index is written to a JSON file at search/search_index.json in the site_dir. The JSON object contained within the file may contain up to three objects.

{
    config: {...},
    docs: [...],
    index: {...}
}

If present, the config object contains the key/value pairs of config options defined for the plugin in the user's mkdocs.yml config file under plugings.search. The config object was new in MkDocs version 1.0.

The docs object contains a list of document objects. Each document object is made up of a location (URL), a title, and text which can be used to create a search index and/or display search results.

If present, the index object contains a pre-built index which offers performance improvements for larger sites. Note that the pre-built index is only created if the user explicitly enables the prebuild_index config option. Themes should expect the index to not be present, but can choose to use the index when it is available. The index object was new in MkDocs version 1.0.

docs.title: Packaging Themes
docs.text:
MkDocs makes use of Python packaging to distribute themes. This comes with a few requirements.

To see an example of a package containing one theme, see the MkDocs Bootstrap theme and to see a package that contains many themes, see the MkDocs Bootswatch theme.

NOTE: It is not strictly necessary to package a theme, as the entire theme can be contained in the custom_dir. If you have created a "one-off theme," that should be sufficient. However, if you intend to distribute your theme for others to use, packaging the theme has some advantages. By packaging your theme, your users can more easily install it, they can rely on a default configuration being defined, and they can then take advantage of the custom_dir to make tweaks to your theme to better suit their needs.

docs.title: Package Layout
docs.text:
The following layout is recommended for themes. Two files at the top level directory called MANIFEST.in and setup.py beside the theme directory which contains an empty __init__.py file, a theme configuration file (mkdocs_theme.yml), and your template and media files.

.
|-- MANIFEST.in
|-- theme_name
|   |-- __init__.py
|   |-- mkdocs_theme.yml
|   |-- main.html
|   |-- styles.css
`-- setup.py

The MANIFEST.in file should contain the following contents but with theme_name updated and any extra file extensions added to the include.

recursive-include theme_name *.ico *.js *.css *.png *.html *.eot *.svg *.ttf *.woff
recursive-exclude * __pycache__
recursive-exclude * *.py[co]

The setup.py should include the following text with the modifications described below.

from setuptools import setup, find_packages

VERSION = '0.0.1'

setup(
    name="mkdocs-themename",
    version=VERSION,
    url='',
    license='',
    description='',
    author='',
    author_email='',
    packages=find_packages(),
    include_package_data=True,
    entry_points={
        'mkdocs.themes': [
            'themename = theme_name',
        ]
    },
    zip_safe=False
)

Fill in the URL, license, description, author and author email address.

The name should follow the convention mkdocs-themename (like mkdocs-bootstrap and mkdocs-bootswatch), starting with MkDocs, using hyphens to separate words and including the name of your theme.

Most of the rest of the file can be left unedited. The last section we need to change is the entry_points. This is how MkDocs finds the theme(s) you are including in the package. The name on the left is the one that users will use in their mkdocs.yml and the one on the right is the directory containing your theme files.

The directory you created at the start of this section with the main.html file should contain all of the other theme files. The minimum requirement is that it includes a main.html for the theme. It must also include a __init__.py file which should be empty, this file tells Python that the directory is a package.

docs.title: Theme Configuration
docs.text:
A packaged theme is required to include a configuration file named mkdocs_theme.yml which is placed in the root of your template files. The file should contain default configuration options for the theme. However, if the theme offers no configuration options, the file is still required and can be left blank. A theme which is not packaged does not need a mkdocs_theme.yml file as that file is not loaded from theme.custom_dir.

The theme author is free to define any arbitrary options deemed necessary and those options will be made available in the templates to control behavior. For example, a theme might want to make a sidebar optional and include the following in the mkdocs_theme.yml file:

show_sidebar: true

Then in a template, that config option could be referenced:

{% if config.theme.show_sidebar %}
<div id="sidebar">...</div>
{% endif %}

And the user could override the default in their project's mkdocs.yml config file:

theme:
    name: themename
    show_sidebar: false

In addition to arbitrary options defined by the theme, MkDocs defines a few special options which alters its behavior:

BLOCK:

Plugins may also define some options which allow the theme to inform a plugin about which set of plugin options it expects. See the documentation for any plugins you may wish to support in your theme.

docs.title: locale
docs.text:
This option mirrors the theme config option of the same name. If this value is not defined in the mkdocs_theme.yml file and the user does not set it in mkdocs.yml then it will default to en (English). The value is expected to match the language used in the text provided by the theme (such a "next" and "previous" links) and should be used as the value of the <html> tag's lang attribute. See Supporting theme localization/ translation for more information.

Note that during configuration validation, the provided string is converted to a Locale object. The object contains Locale.language and Locale.territory attributes and will resolve as a string from within a template. Therefore, the following will work fine:

<html lang="{ config.theme.locale }">

If the locale was set to fr_CA (Canadian French), then the above template would render as:

<html lang="fr_CA">

If you did not want the territory attribute to be included, then reference the language attribute directly:

<html lang="{ config.theme.locale.language }">

That would render as:

<html lang="fr">

docs.title: static_templates
docs.text: This option mirrors the theme config option of the same name and allows some defaults to be set by the theme. Note that while the user can add templates to this list, the user cannot remove templates included in the theme's config.

docs.title: extends
docs.text: Defines a parent theme that this theme inherits from. The value should be the string name of the parent theme. Normal Jinja inheritance rules apply.

docs.title: Distributing Themes
docs.text:
With the above changes, your theme should now be ready to install. This can be done with pip, using pip install . if you are still in the same directory as the setup.py.

Most Python packages, including MkDocs, are distributed on PyPI. To do this, you should run the following command.

python setup.py register

If you don't have an account setup, you should be prompted to create one.

For a much more detailed guide, see the official Python packaging documentation for Packaging and Distributing Projects.

docs.title: Supporting theme Localization/Translation
docs.text:
While the built-in themes provide support for localization/translation of templates, custom themes and third-party themes may choose not to. Regardless, the locale setting of the theme configuration option is always present and is relied upon by other parts of the system. Therefore, it is recommended that all third-party themes use the same setting for designating a language regardless of the system they use for translation. In that way, users will experience consistent behavior regardless of the theme they may choose.

The method for managing translations is up to the developers of a theme. However, if a theme developer chooses to use the same mechanisms used by the built-in themes, the sections below outline how to enable and make use of the same commands utilized by MkDocs.

docs.title: Using the Localization/Translation commands
docs.text:
WARNING: As pybabel is not installed by default and most users will not have pybabel installed, theme developers and/or translators should make sure to have installed the necessary dependencies (using pip install mkdocs[i18n]) in order for the commands to be available for use.

The translation commands should be called from the root of your theme's working tree.

For an overview of the workflow used by MkDocs to translate the built-in themes, see the appropriate section of the Contributing Guide and the Translation Guide.

docs.title: Example custom theme Localization/Translation workflow
docs.text:
NOTE: If your theme inherits from an existing theme which already provides translation catalogs, your theme's translations will be merged with the parent theme's translations during a MkDocs build.

This means that you only need to concentrate on the added translations. Yet, you will still benefit from the translations of the parent theme. At the same time, you may override any of parent theme's translations!

Let's suppose that you're working on your own fork of the mkdocs-basic-theme and want to add translations to it.

Edit the templates by wrapping text in your HTML sources with {% trans %} and {% endtrans %} as follows:

--- a/basic_theme/base.html
+++ b/basic_theme/base.html
@@ -88,7 +88,7 @@

 <body>

-  <h1>This is an example theme for MkDocs.</h1>
+  <h1>{% trans %}This is an example theme for MkDocs.{% endtrans %}</h1>

   <p>
     It is designed to be read by looking at the theme HTML which is heavily

Then you would follow the Translation Guide as usual to get your translations running.

docs.title: Packaging Translations with your theme
docs.text:
While the Portable Object Template (pot) file created by the extract_messages command and the Portable Object (po) files created by the init_catalog and update_catalog commands are useful for creating and editing translations, they are not used by MkDocs directly and do not need to be included in a packaged release of a theme. When MkDocs builds a site with translations, it only makes use of the binary mo files(s) for the specified locale. Therefore, when packaging a theme, make sure to include it in the "wheels", using a MANIFEST.in file or otherwise.

Then, before building your Python package, you will want to ensure that the binary mo file for each locale is up-to-date by running the compile_catalog command for each locale. MkDocs expects the binary mo files to be located at locales/<locale>/LC_MESSAGES/messages.mo, which the compile_catalog command automatically does for you. See Testing theme translations for details.

NOTE: As outlined in our Translation Guide, the MkDocs project has chosen to include the pot and po files in our code repository, but not the mo files. This requires us to always run compile_catalog before packaging a new release regardless of whether any changes were made to a translation or not. However, you may chose an alternate workflow for your theme. At a minimum, you need to ensure that up-to-date mo files are included at the correct location in each release. However, you may use a different process for generating those mo files if you chose to do so.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text:
about/contributing.md# Translations

Theme localization guide.

The built-in themes that are included with MkDocs provide support for translations. This is a guide for translators, which documents the process for contributing new translations and/or updating existing translations. For guidance on modifying the existing themes, see the Contributing Guide. To enable a specific translation see the documentation about the specific theme you are using in the User Guide. For translations of third-party themes, please see the documentation for those themes. For a third-party theme to make use of MkDocs' translation tools and methods, that theme must be properly configured to make use of those tools.

NOTE: Translations only apply to text contained within a theme's template, such as "next" and "previous" links. The Markdown content of a page is not translated. If you wish to create multilingual documentation, you need to combine theme localization with a third-party internationalization/localization plugin.

docs.title: Localization tooling prerequisites
docs.text:
Theme localization makes use of the babel project for generation and compilation of localization files. You will need to be working from the git working tree on your local machine to make use of the translation commands.

See the Contributing Guide for direction on how to Install for Development and Submit a Pull Request. The instructions in this document assume that you are working from a properly configured development environment.

Make sure translation requirements are installed in your environment:

pip install mkdocs[i18n]

docs.title: Adding language translations to themes
docs.text:
If your favorite language locale is not yet supported on one (or both) of the built-in themes (mkdocs and readthedocs), you can easily contribute a translation by following the steps below.

Here is a quick summary of what you'll need to do:

  1. Fork and clone the MkDocs repository and then install MkDocs for development for adding and testing translations.
  2. Initialize new localization catalogs for your language (if a translation for your locale already exists, follow the instructions for updating theme localization files instead).
  3. Add a translation for every text placeholder in the localized catalogs.
  4. Locally serve and test the translated themes for your language.
  5. Update the documentation about supported translations for each translated theme.
  6. Contribute your translation through a Pull Request.

NOTE: Translation locales are usually identified using the ISO-639-1 (2-letter) language codes. While territory/region/county codes are also supported, location specific translations should only be added after the general language translation has been completed and the regional dialect requires use of a term which differs from the general language translation.

docs.title: Fork and clone the MkDocs repository
docs.text:
In the following steps you'll work with a fork of the MkDocs repository. Follow the instructions for forking and cloning the MkDocs repository.

To test the translations you also need to install MkDocs for development from your fork.

docs.title: Initializing the localization catalogs
docs.text:
The templates for each theme contain text placeholders that have been extracted into a Portable Object Template (messages.pot) file, which is present in each theme's folder.

Initializing a catalog consists of running a command which will create a directory structure for your desired language and prepare a Portable Object (messages.po) file derived from the pot file of the theme.

Use the init_catalog command on each theme's directory and provide the appropriate language code (-l <language>).

The language code is almost always just two lowercase letters, such as sv, but in some cases it needs to be further disambiguated.

See:

  • Already translated languages for built-in themes
  • ISO 639 Language List
  • Language subtag registry

In particular, the way to know that the pt language should be disambiguated as pt_PT and pt_BR is that the Language subtag registry page contains pt- if you search for it. Whereas sv should remain just sv, because that page does not contain sv-.

So, if we pick es (Spanish) as our example language code, to add a translation for it to both built-in themes, run these commands:

pybabel init --input-file mkdocs/themes/mkdocs/messages.pot --output-dir mkdocs/themes/mkdocs/locales -l es
pybabel init --input-file mkdocs/themes/readthedocs/messages.pot --output-dir mkdocs/themes/readthedocs/locales -l es

The above command will create a file structure as follows:

mkdocs/themes/mkdocs/locales
├── es
│   └── LC_MESSAGES
│       └── messages.po

You can now move on to the next step and add a translation for every text placeholder in the localized catalog.

docs.title: Updating a theme translation
docs.text:
If a theme's messages.pot template file has been updated since the messages.po was last updated for your locale, follow the steps below to update the theme's messages.po file:

  1. Update the theme's translation catalog to refresh the translatable text placeholders of each theme.
  2. Translate the newly added translatable text placeholders on every messages.po catalog file language you can.
  3. Locally serve and test the translated themes for your language.
  4. Contribute your translation through a Pull Request.

docs.title: Updating the translation catalogs
docs.text:
This step should be completed after a theme template have been updated for each language that you are comfortable contributing a translation for.

To update the fr translation catalog of both built-in themes, use the following commands:

pybabel update --ignore-obsolete --update-header-comment --input-file mkdocs/themes/mkdocs/messages.pot --output-dir mkdocs/themes/mkdocs/locales -l fr
pybabel update --ignore-obsolete --update-header-comment --input-file mkdocs/themes/readthedocs/messages.pot --output-dir mkdocs/themes/readthedocs/locales -l fr

You can now move on to the next step and add a translation for every updated text placeholder in the localized catalog.

docs.title: Translating the MkDocs themes
docs.text:
Now that your localized messages.po files are ready, all you need to do is add a translation in each msgstr item for each msgid item in the file.

msgid "Next"
msgstr "Siguiente"

WARNING: Do not modify the msgid as it is common to all translations. Just add its translation in the msgstr item.

Once you have finished translating all of the terms listed in the po file, you'll want to test your localized theme.

docs.title: Testing theme translations
docs.text:
To test a theme with translations, you need to first compile the messages.po files of your theme into messages.mo files. The following commands will compile the es translation for both built-in themes:

pybabel compile --statistics --directory mkdocs/themes/mkdocs/locales -l es
pybabel compile --statistics --directory mkdocs/themes/readthedocs/locales -l es

The above command results in the following file structure:

mkdocs/themes/mkdocs/locales
├── es
│   └── LC_MESSAGES
│       ├── messages.mo
│       └── messages.po

Note that the compiled messages.mo file was generated based on the messages.po file that you just edited.

Then modify the mkdocs.yml file at the root of the project to test the new and/or updated locale:

theme:
    name: mkdocs
    locale: es

Finally, run mkdocs serve to check out your new localized version of the theme.

NOTE: The build and release process takes care of compiling and distributing all locales to end users so you only have to worry about contributing the actual text translation messages.po files (the rest is ignored by git).

After you have finished testing your work, be sure to undo the change to the locale setting in the mkdocs.yml file before submitting your changes.

docs.title: Updating theme documentation
docs.text: Update the lists of supported translations for each translated theme located at Choosing your theme (docs/user-guide/choosing-your-theme.md), in their locale options.

docs.title: Contributing translations
docs.text: It is now time for you to contribute your nice work to the project. Thank you!

docs.title: 1000 问知识体系｜Flomo 汇总入口
docs.text: 将 Flomo 中围绕「1000 问 / 1000 个问题 / 堆问题学习法」的知识资产集中到 Wiki，作为长期维护的总目录。原始 Flomo 笔记保留为来源与追溯入口；本页负责统一导航、学习方法、专题边界和后续沉淀规则。

docs.title: 核心方法：先提出问题，再组织答案
docs.text:
堆问题学习法不是一次性写出 1000 个完美问题，而是先建立领域问题地图，再按知识结构、难度和关联逐步回答。

  1. 选领域与边界：明确目标、使用场景和知识范围。
  2. 建立问题地图：先铺开基础概念、原理、机制、工程实践、故障排查与演进趋势。
  3. 分层分类：按专题归档；避免问题只按产生时间堆积。
  4. 逐题回答：回答应包含结论、原理、示例/证据、适用边界和常见误区；暂时不会的标记待查。
  5. 建立双向链接：关联先修知识、工程案例、代码、规范与其他问题。
  6. 实践验证：通过实验、项目、测试或真实案例验证答案。
  7. 周期回顾：补充新问题、合并重复问题、修正过时答案，并记录验证日期。

docs.title: 两类问题设计
docs.text:
• 深挖型（技术树）：面向 AUTOSAR、C、嵌入式等专业领域。重点追问 Why / How、边界条件、时序、异常路径、工具行为和量产故障。
  • 铺开型（知识面）：面向历史、文化、通识等领域。先建立 What / Who / When / Where 的全景，再逐步深入原因、影响与争议。
  • 考试型：数学、软考等先按课程体系建立定义、定理、关系和典型题，再补应用题；不机械地把“先列 1000 问”套用于所有学科。

docs.title: 专题导航
docs.text:
专题 范围与组织建议 Flomo 原始入口 AUTOSAR 1000 问 Classic / Adaptive、架构、RTE/SWC、通信栈、网络管理、诊断、NvM、OS、多核、安全、信息安全、工具链、ARXML、生成代码、集成与量产排障 AUTOSAR 1000 问总表 嵌入式 1000 问 MCU/MPU、处理器架构、存储与链接、GPIO/外设、中断、定时器、DMA、低功耗、RTOS、Bootloader、嵌入式 Linux、调试、通信、性能 嵌入式 1000 问全景 C 语言 1000 问 语法与类型、指针与内存、编译链接、多文件组织、预处理、标准库、未定义行为、嵌入式 C、MISRA、工程调试 C 语言导航 硬件 / 电气工程 1000 问 电源与保护、模拟/数字电路、传感器、ADC、信号完整性、接口电路、测量与故障定位 硬件专题导航 AI 1000 问 AI 基础、大模型、Embedding/RAG、Agent、模型部署、AI 与知识管理、端侧 AI、视频理解与生成 AI 1000 问全景 考研数学 1000 问 高等数学、线性代数、概率论；按定义/关系、定理推导、典型题、工程应用分层 考研数学 1000 问导航；概率论分卷 软考 / 系统架构师 1000 问 计算机体系结构、操作系统、网络、数据库、软件工程、架构设计、案例分析与论文 软考 1000 问 历史 1000 问 历史主干与专题分卷；建立时间线、制度、人物、因果链与史料来源 历史专栏导航 儿童教育 1000 问 儿童发展、学习习惯、亲子沟通、教育方法与实际场景；区分证据、经验和个人判断 儿童教育 1000 问 MATLAB 1000 问 MATLAB 基础、数值计算、数据可视化、信号处理、Simulink、工程建模与调试 待从 Flomo 对应专题导航补齐 电气工程 1000 问 电路基础、电机与电力电子、控制、测量、工程安全与应用场景 需继续检索并补齐原始总表 通识 / 传统文化 以问题地图作为入口，先铺开范围，再按专题深入；记录来源与不同观点 需继续检索并补齐原始总表

注意：上表中的 Flomo 链接是原始笔记入口。Wiki 中的目录是汇总与导航，不意味着每个专题的所有答案已经完成；原始内容应继续逐条迁移和去重。

docs.title: AUTOSAR 1000 问：专题地图
docs.text:
• 基础与架构：AUTOSAR 的目标、分层、RTE、SW-C、VFB、配置与代码生成。
  • 通信栈：Signal/PDU、COM、PduR、CanIf、CanTp、CAN/LIN/FlexRay、SOME/IP、DoIP、CAN FD/XL。
  • 网络管理与 ECU 状态：EcuM、BswM、ComM、CanNm、唤醒、休眠、Partial Networking。
  • 诊断：Dcm、UDS、DID、DTC/DEM、诊断会话、安全访问、刷写、CAN TP 与 DoIP。
  • 非易失存储：NvM、MemIf、Fee、Fls、Block 类型、掉电一致性、写入策略。
  • OS 与多核：任务/中断、Schedule Table、IOC、Spinlock、内存保护、核间通信。
  • 功能安全与信息安全：ISO 26262、ASIL、E2E、WdgM、SecOC、Crypto、HSM、OTA 与回滚。
  • 工具链与工程化：DaVinci、EB tresos、ARXML、配置依赖、Pre-Compile/Link/Post-Build、生成代码审查、CI。
  • 运行时排障：报文不发送、周期抖动、RTE 数据不刷新、Bus-Off、初始化顺序、链接失败。
  • 平台演进与集成：Classic/Adaptive、Linux 共存、ROS 2 对比、版本迁移、变体管理、测试与验证。

docs.title: 嵌入式 1000 问：专题地图
docs.text:
• 基础概念与处理器架构
  • 存储器、内存布局、链接脚本与启动流程
  • GPIO、UART、I²C、SPI、ADC、PWM、定时器
  • 中断、异常、临界区与实时性
  • DMA、低功耗、看门狗与可靠性
  • 裸机、RTOS、任务同步、死锁与性能分析
  • Bootloader、升级、分区与掉电恢复
  • 嵌入式 Linux、设备树、驱动与上下半部
  • CAN/LIN/CAN FD 等通信协议
  • JTAG/SWD、HardFault、示波器、逻辑分析仪与系统调试
  • 硬件—软件边界、信号完整性与工程验证

docs.title: 从 Flomo 到 Wiki 的沉淀规则
docs.text:
每个问题建议使用统一结构：

  1. 问题：一句话表达具体疑问。
  2. 简答：先给结论，再解释原因。
  3. 原理 / 流程：必要时用 Mermaid 图、时序图或分层图。
  4. 示例：代码、配置片段、报文、公式或真实案例。
  5. 边界与误区：说明版本、平台、前提和容易误判的地方。
  6. 验证方式：测试方法、实验步骤、规范章节或可信来源。
  7. 关联问题：链接到先修问题、相邻专题和工程案例。
  8. 来源与状态：保留 Flomo 原文链接，标注“待回答 / 初稿 / 已验证 / 需更新”。

docs.title: 去重与迁移原则
docs.text:
• 不删除 Flomo 原笔记；Wiki 是整理后的知识库，Flomo 是原始捕获与历史来源。
  • 相同问题只保留一个主条目；其他版本作为补充、案例或来源链接。
  • 不把“问题清单”误标成“已回答”；答案和验证状态分开记录。
  • 保留原始术语、标准版本、时间和工程上下文；遇到相互矛盾的答案时记录差异，不强行合并。
  • 每个专题维护一个索引页；避免把所有内容挤进单一超长页面。
  • 采用相对路径链接，方便 GitHub 浏览及后续迁移到个人 Wiki/数字花园。

docs.title: 来源与方法论笔记
docs.text:
• 堆问题学习法：先列问题、分类、逐一回答、重复问题继续深挖、定期回顾。
  • 我的知识管理体系总览：输入 → 整理 → 存储 → 输出 → 实践 → 反馈的循环。
  • AI 与知识管理：从 1000 问到个人知识库闭环：将问题库、卡片笔记和 AI 整理流程连接起来。
  • 1000 问：技术树深挖与知识面铺开的区别：不同领域采用不同的问题设计策略。

▎1000 问全景（问题库）

▎ 基础概念

  1. "人工智能"、"机器学习"、"深度学习"这三个概念之间的关系是什么样的？用一张包含关系图怎么画？

  2. 图灵测试是什么？如果一个AI通过了图灵测试，它真的"理解"了吗？还是只是装得像在理解？

  3. "强AI"和"弱AI"的区别是什么？现在用的ChatGPT、Midjourney属于哪一种？

  4. 人工智能历史上经历了三次"寒冬"和两次"春天"——每次寒冬的触发因素是什么？每次春天又是因为什么突破？

▎ 机器学习基础

  1. 什么是"监督学习"、"无监督学习"、"半监督学习"、"强化学习"？它们的核心区别在于训练时有没有"标签"？

  2. "过拟合"是什么意思？一个模型在训练集上准确率99%、在测试集上只有60%——这个差距说明了什么？

  3. "欠拟合"和"过拟合"的平衡——模型太简单会欠拟合、太复杂会过拟合，中间那个点怎么找到？

  4. 训练集、验证集、测试集——三个集合各有什么用？为什么不能拿测试集来做模型选择？

▎ 深度学习基础

  1. 一个神经网络最基本的组成单元是什么？一个"神经元"在数学上做了什么操作——加权求和+激活函数？

  2. 为什么神经网络需要"激活函数"？如果激活函数是线性的（f(x)=x），再多层也能合并成一层——能理解这个问题吗？

  3. ReLU、Sigmoid、Tanh——三种激活函数各有什么优缺点？为什么ReLU在深度网络里比Sigmoid更常用？

  4. 反向传播（backpropagation）的直觉是什么？链式法则在这里起了什么作用？

▎ 监督学习算法

  1. 线性回归为什么叫"线性"？如果数据不是线性的（比如抛物线形状），线性回归还能用吗？

  2. 逻辑回归（Logistic Regression）名字里带"回归"，但做的是分类任务——它到底回归了什么？

  3. 决策树是怎么做分类的？根节点选哪个特征来分裂——选择标准是什么？

  4. 支持向量机（SVM）的"间隔最大化"是什么意思？为什么它要找离两类数据最远的那条分界线？

  5. k近邻（k-NN）为什么是"懒学习"？训练阶段不需要做什么，预测时反而要大量计算——合理吗？

▎ 模型评估

  1. 准确率（Accuracy）在什么情况下会骗人？一个99%准确率的癌症检测模型，如果发病率只有1%，它可能什么都没检测出来——为什么？

  2. 精确率（Precision）和召回率（Recall）的区别是什么？搜索引擎更关心哪个？

  3. F1分数为什么是精确率和召回率的"调和平均"而不是算术平均？什么时候该用F1而不是单独用P或R？

  4. ROC曲线和AUC——ROC曲线画的是什么？AUC=0.5意味着什么、AUC=1.0又意味着什么？

▎ 优化方法

  1. 梯度下降（Gradient Descent）的直觉是什么？沿着梯度反方向走为什么能找到最小值？

  2. 学习率太大了会怎样？太小了呢？有没有"自适应"的学习率方法？

  3. 随机梯度下降（SGD）和批量梯度下降（Batch GD）的区别是什么？SGD一次只看一个样本就更新参数——这样参数会不会"乱跳"？

  4. 什么是"局部最优"和"全局最优"？在非凸函数的优化里，梯度下降会被困在局部最优吗？

▎ 无监督学习

  1. K-means聚类是怎么工作的？"K"代表什么？为什么需要先确定K？

  2. K-means的"初始质心"怎么选？选不好会怎么样？

  3. 主成分分析（PCA）在做什么？为什么说它"找数据里方差最大的方向"？这个方向和"保留最多信息"有什么关系？

▎ 神经网络架构——CNN

  1. 卷积层（Convolution）在图像上做了什么操作？一个3×3卷积核和一个5×5卷积核的区别是什么？

  2. 池化（Pooling）层有什么用？最大池化和平均池化各自提取了什么特征？

  3. 卷积神经网络为什么比全连接网络更适合处理图像？"平移不变性"和"局部连接"在这起了什么作用？

▎ 神经网络架构——RNN / 序列模型

  1. 循环神经网络（RNN）是怎么处理序列数据的？为什么说它的"隐藏状态"在记忆之前的信息？

  2. RNN的"梯度消失"问题是怎么产生的？为什么长句子RNN记不住开头的信息？

  3. LSTM（长短期记忆网络）的三个门（遗忘门、输入门、输出门）各在控制什么？为什么它能记住远距离的信息？

▎ NLP / 词嵌入基础

  1. Word2Vec是怎么把"单词"变成"向量"的？为什么"国王-男人+女人≈女王"能成立？

▎ 计算机视觉基础

  1. 图像分类任务里，一张224×224的彩色图片在计算机里是几个数？如果输入到神经网络，第一层要处理多少参数？

▎ Transformer 与注意力机制

  1. 注意力机制（Attention）的直觉是什么——"在翻译一句话时，模型不应该平等地看所有词，而是应该关注当前输出位置最相关的输入词"——它的数学表达 Q、K、V 三个矩阵分别代表什么？

  2. Transformer 的"自注意力"（Self-Attention）和 RNN 在处理序列上的本质区别是什么？为什么说 Transformer 是"并行"而 RNN 是"串行"的——这个并行带来了什么好处？

  3. Transformer 里的位置编码（Positional Encoding）为什么需要？既然输入是并行处理的，模型怎么知道哪个词在前、哪个词在后？

▎ 大语言模型（LLM）基础

  1. GPT 的"自回归"（Autoregressive）是什么意思——生成下一个词时，它能看到哪些词？这和 BERT 的"双向"有什么本质不同？

  2. 什么是"涌现能力"（Emergent Abilities）？为什么 7B 的模型不会做算术，70B 的模型突然会了——这个"突然"是哪来的？

  3. 为什么大模型需要"上下文窗口"（context window）的限制？如果一次给它输入 10 万字的对话，为什么它会"忘掉"开头说了什么？

▎ 强化学习基础

  1. 强化学习里的"智能体"（Agent）、"环境"（Environment）、"动作"（Action）、"奖励"（Reward）四个要素是什么关系？AlphaGo 下围棋——每一步落子是 Action，赢了是 Reward（+1），这是一个什么过程？

  2. 强化学习里的"探索"（Exploration）和"利用"（Exploitation）的权衡是什么？一个扫地机器人总是在同一个角落转（利用它已知的最好路径）和去新区域试试（探索）——怎么决定什么时候试新路？

▎ 集成学习（Bagging / Boosting）

  1. 随机森林（Random Forest）是怎么通过"多个弱分类器组合成一个强分类器"的？为什么每棵树只用部分数据和部分特征，结果反而比一棵全数据的决策树好？

  2. XGBoost 和随机森林在"构建多棵树"时的理念有什么不同——一个并行建树再投票（Bagging），一个串行建树、每棵新树纠正前一棵的错（Boosting）？

▎ 生成式模型（GAN / VAE / 扩散模型）

  1. 生成对抗网络（GAN）的"生成器"和"判别器"在玩一个什么游戏？生成器画假画，判别器鉴定真假——为什么这个博弈能训练出能画逼真人脸的生成器？

  2. Stable Diffusion 这类"扩散模型"的原理直觉是什么——从一个全是噪声的图片开始，一步步"去噪"直到变成一张清晰的猫的图片？每一步去掉一点噪声，这个"去噪"过程是谁教给模型的？

▎ 迁移学习与微调

  1. ImageNet 上预训练好的 ResNet 模型，被迁移到"X光胸片分类"任务上——前几层（识别边缘、纹理）不用重学，只需要在最后几层重新训练——为什么前几层的特征是"通用的"？

  2. "全量微调"和"LoRA（低秩适配）"微调的区别是什么？为什么 LoRA 只需要训练参数量 0.1% 的权重就能达到接近全量微调的效果？

▎ 模型可解释性

  1. 深度模型经常被说成"黑箱"——可解释性方法 LIME 和 SHAP 各自怎么解释一个模型为什么把某张图片分类为"猫"？LIME 在图片的局部区域加模糊，看分类结果变化；SHAP 根据每个像素对最终判断的贡献分配"重要性分数"——两个思路有什么不同？

▎ 推荐系统基础

  1. 协同过滤（Collaborative Filtering）和基于内容的推荐（Content-based）的本质区别是什么？Amazon 的"买了这个商品的用户也买了..."是哪种？

  2. 推荐系统里的"冷启动"（Cold Start）问题是什么？一个新用户没有任何行为记录，一个新商品没有任何用户评价——推荐系统怎么给它们推荐？

▎ 目标检测与语义分割

  1. 图像分类、目标检测、语义分割——三个任务的输出分别是什么？分类输出"猫"，检测输出"猫在 (x,y,w,h)"，分割输出"图片里每一个像素属于猫还是背景"——哪一步最难？

  2. YOLO（You Only Look Once）为什么叫这个名字？它把目标检测当成一个"回归问题"——输入一张图，直接输出所有边界框的位置和类别，一步到位，跟 R-CNN 两阶段方法的区别在哪？

▎ 图神经网络（GNN）

  1. 图神经网络在解决什么问题？社交网络里的每个人是一个节点，朋友关系是一条边——如果只给部分节点标注了"高消费用户"，怎么预测其他节点是否高消费？

  2. GNN 的"消息传递"（Message Passing）是什么意思？每个节点收齐邻居的信息，"更新"自己的特征——重复几轮后，相隔两跳的节点也能互相影响吗？

▎ 自监督学习与对比学习

  1. 自监督学习（Self-Supervised Learning）为什么叫"自"监督——数据没有人类标注的标签，模型自己给自己造"伪标签"来学习。在 NLP 里 BERT 的做法是"盖住一些词让模型猜"，这跟"有监督学习"有什么不同？

  2. 对比学习（Contrastive Learning）的核心思想是什么——"让同一张猫的两张不同变换（裁剪、旋转）后的图片在特征空间里靠近，让不同图片远离"？这个"拉近同类、推远异类"的训练目标跟分类的交叉熵损失比，优势在哪？

▎ 模型部署与推理优化

  1. 训练好的 PyTorch 模型要部署到手机或服务器上，为什么要"导出"成 ONNX 或 TensorRT 格式？直接用 PyTorch 的 .pt 文件跑推理不行吗？

  2. 模型量化（Quantization）把 float32 变成 int8 后，模型大小变成原来的四分之一，推理速度大幅提升——但精度为什么几乎不掉？这是因为神经网络对噪声的"鲁棒性"吗？

▎ AI伦理与公平性

  1. 人脸识别系统对不同肤色人群的准确率不同——这个"偏差"来自哪里？是模型的偏见还是训练数据分布不均匀？

  2. 一个银行的贷款审批模型，训练数据里过去批准的大多数贷款给了男性，模型学会把"性别"作为重要特征——怎么检测并消除这个偏见？用"性别"这个敏感属性不能作为输入就能解决吗？

▎ 语音与音频处理基础

  1. 语音识别（ASR）的第一步通常是把声音信号变成频谱图（Mel频谱）——为什么原始波形不好直接用？人耳对频率的感知不是线性的，Mel 刻度就是模拟了这个非线性特性？

  2. 文本到语音（TTS）是怎么让合成的语音听起来不像机器人的？现在的主流 TTS（如 Tacotron、VITS）的核心思路是"从文本到频谱再到波形"——中间的频谱怎么反过来变成声音？

▎ 强化学习深入（Q-Learning / DQN）

  1. Q-Learning 的 Q 值代表什么？"Q(s, a)"——在一个状态 s 下执行动作 a，未来能获得的总回报期望。为什么 Q 值不是一个数而是一张"状态×动作"的表？当状态空间连续（比如机器人关节角度）时，这张表存不下怎么办？

  2. Deep Q-Network（DQN）用神经网络代替了 Q 表——输入是状态，输出是每个动作的 Q 值。那 DQN 怎么解决"用网络当前预测的 Q 值来更新网络自身"这个循环依赖问题？"目标网络"（Target Network）在这做了什么？

  3. Policy Gradient 方法和 Q-Learning 的思维方式本质区别是什么？一个直接学"在每个状态选什么动作最好"，另一个学"每个动作值多少钱"，然后根据值来选——PPO 为什么在实践中比 DQN 更稳定？

▎ RAG（检索增强生成）

  1. RAG 的核心链路是：用户提问 → 把问题转成向量 → 从向量数据库里检索最相关的几段文本 → 把检索到的文本拼到 prompt 里 → LLM 回答。为什么说 RAG 解决了 LLM 的"知识截止日期"和"幻觉"两个问题？它跟直接把大段资料塞进上下文的做法有什么不同？

  2. RAG 里的"分块策略"（chunking）——一段 500 页的 PDF，是按每 256 个字切块、还是按段落切块、还是按语义切块？如果切得太碎，检索回来的片段说了一半的话没有上下文；切得太大，一个块里混合了多个主题。怎么找到中间的平衡点？

▎ AI Agent / 工具使用

  1. 一个"AI Agent"和普通的 LLM 聊天有什么区别？Agent 的核心是"能自己决定调用工具"——比如问天气，Agent 不直接回答，而是决定去调用天气 API——这个"决定调用哪个函数"的行为是什么机制控制的？

  2. ReAct（Reasoning + Acting）模式是怎么工作的？Agent 收到问题后，不是一步给出答案，而是"想一下 → 查一下 → 再想想 → 再查一下"的循环，直到有足够信息才回答——这个"思考-行动-观察"的循环跟人类解决问题的流程有什么相似之处？

▎ 向量数据库与嵌入搜索

  1. 向量数据库存的是什么？不是存原始文本，而是存"文本的语义向量"——"猫追老鼠"和"猫咪在抓耗子"两句话的向量距离很近。那么问题来了：怎么把"语义相似"映射成"向量距离近"？这个映射是谁训练的？

  2. 向量数据库做搜索时的"近似最近邻"（ANN）和传统的"精确最近邻"有什么区别？一个 100 万条向量精确找最近的 10 条，逐条比对太慢——ANN 通过牺牲一点精度（比如只找到 95% 的正确答案）来换取千倍的速度提升，它用了什么数据结构？

▎ 时间序列分析与预测

  1. 时间序列预测跟普通回归预测的本质区别是什么？普通回归假设样本相互独立，但今天的气温和昨天的气温是高度相关的——时间序列预测的核心是捕捉这个"时间依赖结构"。ARIMA 模型怎么通过"自回归"（AR）和"滑动平均"（MA）两种成分来描述时间序列？

  2. LSTM 在时间序列预测里跟传统统计方法（ARIMA、指数平滑）比，有什么不可替代的优势？如果一个任务是预测明天某个化工反应釜的温度——历史数据有 3 年的每小时记录，数据有明显的季节性模式和偶尔的异常波动——LSTM 能比 ARIMA 多抓住什么？

▎ AutoML 与超参数优化

  1. 手动调参的问题在哪？一个 XGBoost 模型有十几个超参数，每个参数连续取值——搜索空间是天文数字。网格搜索（Grid Search）为什么在这个场景下不可行？

  2. 贝叶斯优化（Bayesian Optimization）是怎么用更少的试验次数找到好超参数的？它给每个超参数组合一个"期望分数"和"不确定性"——每次选那些"可能好但不确定"的参数来试，而不是"确定好但已经试过的"。为什么这个策略比随机搜索高效？

▎ 多模态学习（Vision + Language）

  1. CLIP 模型是怎么同时理解图片和文字的？OpenAI 用 4 亿张（图片，文字描述）对来训练——让"一张猫的图片"的向量和"一只橘猫在晒太阳"的文本向量靠近，跟不匹配的图片-文本对远离。训练完后，怎么用 CLIP 做"零样本分类"——给它一张它没见过的品种的狗的照片，它怎么猜出这是"狗"？

  2. 多模态大模型（如 GPT-4V、LLaVA）是怎么实现"看图说话"的？一个典型的做法是把图片切成 patch，用视觉编码器（如 ViT）把每个 patch 转成向量，然后把图像向量序列当 prompt 拼到文本 token 前面——这样 LLM 就能"看到"图片的内容了？这个拼接方式有什么问题？

▎ 知识图谱

  1. 知识图谱的"三元组"（头实体—关系—尾实体）是什么？"北京是中国的首都"三元组化后变成（北京，首都，中国）。知识图谱为什么用这种结构来表示知识——如果用关系数据库的表来存，跟三元组比差在哪？

  2. 知识图谱的"补全"（Knowledge Graph Completion）是在解决什么问题？知识图谱通常是不完整的——如果已知（姚明，妻子，___）缺了尾实体，怎么用已有的三元组推断出缺失的部分？TransE 模型的思路是把每个实体和关系都投影到向量空间，通过"头实体向量+关系向量≈尾实体向量"来预测缺失联系？

▎ 异常检测（Anomaly Detection）

  1. 异常检测的三种类型——点异常（一个数据点偏离全局分布）、上下文异常（某时刻的数值跟它前后时刻比不对）、集体异常（一组数据一起出现但单独看每个都正常）。

  2. 孤立森林（Isolation Forest）检测异常的原理是什么？正常数据点需要很多次分割才能被"孤立"，异常点只需要很少几次分割就能被孤立出来。

▎ 特征工程与数据预处理

  1. 为什么机器学习模型通常需要"特征缩放"？SVM 和 KNN 依赖距离计算，树模型不需要——为什么？

  2. 类别特征怎么变成数值输入？独热编码导致维度暴涨时，目标编码（Target Encoding）有什么风险和怎么处理？

▎ 联邦学习（Federated Learning）

  1. 联邦学习的核心——数据不出本地，模型参数聚合。客户端上传的是什么参数？服务器怎么做聚合？

  2. Non-IID 问题——不同机构的数据分布天差地别，简单平均模型为什么可能比单独训练更差？

▎ 小样本学习与零样本学习

  1. Few-shot Learning 的核心——用 5 张图片学会一个新概念？元学习（Meta-Learning）在学什么——"学会如何快速适应"？

  2. MAML——找一个"对变化最敏感"的参数初始点，在新样本上一步梯度更新就能收敛。

▎ 模型剪枝与压缩

  1. 剪枝——把权值接近零的连接剪掉。结构化剪枝和非结构化剪枝各有什么取舍？

  2. 知识蒸馏——学生模型学教师模型的"软输出"，软输出为什么信息量更大？

▎ 端侧 AI

  1. 手机上跑 AI 的核心限制——GPU、内存、功耗、发热。端侧优化策略有哪些？

  2. 苹果 Neural Engine 和 Google TPU 在芯片里怎么加速神经网络计算？

▎ 因果推断

  1. "相关"和"因果"的区别——P(Y|X) vs P(Y|do(X))，do 算子代表主动干预。推荐系统应该用关联还是因果？

▎ 偏差-方差权衡

  1. 高偏差=欠拟合，高方差=过拟合。为什么降低一个必然升高另一个？

▎ 半监督学习

  1. 少量标签+大量无标签数据。自训练（Self-training）用伪标签迭代——会不会让错误自我强化？

▎ 主动学习

  1. 模型主动问人类要标签——不确定性采样为什么比随机选样本标注更高效？

▎ Actor-Critic 与 PPO

  1. Actor-Critic 减去基线为什么能降低方差？

  2. PPO 裁剪目标函数限制策略更新步长——"可以进步，但步子不要迈太大"。

▎ Mamba / 状态空间模型

  1. Mamba 基于 SSM，跟 Self-Attention 处理长序列的方式有什么不同？为什么 Mamba O(n) 而 Transformer O(n²)？

▎ AGI / AI 安全与对齐

  1. 对齐问题——怎么确保超级智能的目标反映人类的真实意图？"可扩展监督"和"可解释性"两条路线各在做什么？

▎ Scaling Laws 与规模定律

  1. Scaling Laws 发现模型性能随规模按幂律增长——这是否意味着"算法创新不再重要了"？

  2. Chinchilla 定律建议参数和数据量按 1:20 配比。为什么实际模型不一定按这个最佳比例来？

▎ 大模型训练详解

  1. 训练为什么分三个阶段——预训练→SFT→RLHF？为什么不能跳过预训练只做 SFT？

  2. RLHF 的奖励模型怎么训练？PPO 用奖励模型分数更新模型——"奖励黑客"（Reward Hacking）风险是什么？

▎ 长上下文技术

  1. FlashAttention 通过分块计算和重计算减少显存——为什么能同时变快和变省？

  2. RoPE（旋转位置编码）怎么同时实现位置编码和远程衰减？为什么比绝对位置编码更适合长上下文？

▎ 混合专家模型（MoE）

  1. MoE 拆成大模型为多个专家，每次只激活几个——Mixtral 8×7B 参数量 56B 但每次只算 14B。这个"参量大但计算少"的设计为什么高效？

  2. 路由（Router）怎么决定 token 给哪个专家？负载不均衡怎么办——load balancing loss 在做什么？

▎ Diffusion 模型深入

  1. 前向加噪→反向去噪。为什么不能直接一步去噪而要分几千步？

  2. Classifier-Free Guidance（CFG）混合条件预测和无条件预测——引导尺度设太高为什么会导致图像失真？

▎ AI for Science

  1. AlphaFold 解决了蛋白质折叠——为什么是"五十年未解难题"？它怎么做到的？

  2. GNoME 发现新材料、GraphCast 做气象预测——AI 在科学领域的共同模式是什么？

▎ 视频理解与生成

  1. 视频理解的核心——时间维度。3D 卷积还是时序注意力？怎么跨帧建模？

  2. Sora 为什么被称为"世界模拟器"而不是视频生成器？它也会犯常识错误——为什么模型只学像素分布不学物理规律？

专栏⑯进度：导航 + 10/10篇 + 补充一~四（共 14 篇）✅ 全部完成

docs.title: Wiki 维护说明
docs.text:
• 原始 Flomo 笔记保留不动。
  • 后续可按子专题拆分页面，避免单页过长。
  • 区分问题清单、初稿答案与已验证答案，并保留参考来源。

docs.title: 专题建设补全｜从问题清单到可执行学习路线
docs.text: 本节在原有 Flomo 问题库基础上补齐学习路径、实践项目、工程工具与验收标准。原始问题清单继续保留，不以本节替代原文。

docs.title: 一、知识地图与学习顺序
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[数学与 Python 基础] --> B[机器学习]
    B --> C[深度学习与 PyTorch]
    C --> D[Transformer 与大语言模型]
    D --> E1[RAG 与知识库]
    D --> E2[微调与模型适配]
    D --> E3[Agent 与工具调用]
    C --> F[计算机视觉 / 语音 / 多模态]
    E1 --> G[评估、部署与监控]
    E2 --> G
    E3 --> G
    F --> G
    G --> H[安全、隐私、成本与持续迭代]
阶段 核心目标 必须掌握的知识 可验收成果 0. 编程与数学 能读懂训练代码和公式 Python、NumPy、线性代数、概率、梯度 实现线性回归与梯度下降 1. 机器学习 建立数据到预测的完整流程 数据切分、特征工程、基线、指标、交叉验证 完成分类/回归项目并写评估报告 2. 深度学习 理解神经网络训练 张量、自动微分、损失函数、优化器、正则化 用 PyTorch 训练并保存模型 3. Transformer/LLM 理解生成模型的基本机制 Token、Embedding、Attention、预训练、SFT、推理 调用模型 API，完成结构化输出任务 4. RAG 构建可追溯的私有知识问答 文档解析、切块、向量检索、重排、引用 回答能引用原文并识别无答案问题 5. Agent 让模型可靠地使用工具 工具 schema、状态机、权限、超时、重试 实现带确认步骤的工具工作流 6. 部署与治理 将原型变成可维护服务 评估集、日志、延迟、成本、隐私、回滚 形成可复现部署和监控清单

docs.title: A. 数学、编程与机器学习基础
docs.text:
• Python 数据处理：NumPy、pandas、Matplotlib、数据清洗、缺失值和异常值。
  • 数学基础：向量与矩阵、矩阵乘法、特征值、条件概率、贝叶斯公式、期望与方差、微积分和链式法则。
  • 经典算法：线性/逻辑回归、决策树、随机森林、梯度提升、SVM、K-means、PCA。
  • 评估方法：训练/验证/测试集、交叉验证、数据泄漏、类别不平衡、置信区间。
  • 实践验收：与多数类/均值等简单基线比较；报告 Accuracy、Precision、Recall、F1、ROC-AUC 或 MAE/RMSE，并解释指标选择。

docs.title: B. 深度学习与模型架构
docs.text:
• 网络基础：前向传播、反向传播、激活函数、初始化、归一化、Dropout、权重衰减。
  • CNN：卷积、感受野、池化、数据增强、迁移学习。
  • 序列模型：RNN、LSTM、GRU、时间序列切分和滚动验证。
  • Transformer：Q/K/V、缩放点积注意力、多头注意力、残差、LayerNorm、位置编码、FFN。
  • 生成模型：自回归语言模型、VAE、GAN、Diffusion；区分训练目标、采样过程和适用任务。
  • 实践验收：记录数据版本、随机种子、超参数、训练曲线和模型权重；比较至少一个简单基线。

docs.title: C. 大语言模型与提示工程
docs.text:
• Tokenizer、上下文窗口、采样温度、Top-p、最大输出长度和停止条件。
  • 预训练、监督微调（SFT）、偏好优化/RLHF 的目的与局限。
  • Prompt 设计：角色、背景、约束、示例、输出 schema、拒答条件。
  • 结构化输出：JSON Schema 校验、类型检查、失败重试和降级策略。
  • 模型选择：质量、延迟、上下文长度、工具能力、隐私要求与总成本综合评估。
  • 实践验收：建立 30–100 条代表性测试样本，比较提示词或模型版本，保存错误案例而不是只挑成功示例。

docs.title: D. RAG 与个人知识库
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[PDF / Markdown / 网页] --> B[解析与清洗]
    B --> C[按标题和语义切块]
    C --> D[元数据与权限]
    D --> E[Embedding]
    E --> F[向量/关键词索引]
    Q[用户问题] --> R[问题改写]
    R --> S[混合检索]
    F --> S
    S --> T[重排与去重]
    T --> U[上下文组装]
    U --> V[LLM 生成]
    V --> W[引用校验与拒答]

关键检查点：

  1. 文档解析是否保留标题、表格、代码块、页码和来源链接。
  2. 切块是否避免把定义、条件和结论切散；重叠窗口不能替代合理的结构切分。
  3. 检索是否同时考虑语义匹配、关键词、元数据过滤与权限边界。
  4. 评估应拆成检索质量（Recall@k、MRR/nDCG）和答案质量（正确性、忠实度、引用准确性）。
  5. 必须测试知识库无答案、文档冲突、过期内容、提示注入和越权检索。
  6. 答案中的引用应能定位到原始文件/章节；检索不到证据时明确说明不确定，不应编造出处。

docs.title: E. Agent、工具调用与工作流
docs.text:
• Agent 不等于“会聊天的模型”：它还需要工具、状态、控制流程、权限和终止条件。
  • 先用确定性工作流解决可预测任务；只有需要动态决策时才增加 Agent 自主性。
  • 工具设计：输入 schema、参数校验、最小权限、幂等性、超时、重试上限和审计日志。
  • 安全边界：把检索到的网页/文件视为不可信数据；模型输出不能直接成为 shell 命令、SQL 或高权限操作。
  • 高风险动作应设置人工确认、预览、撤销机制和操作记录。
  • 实践项目：实现“搜索资料 → 摘要 → 生成草稿 → 检查引用 → 人工确认”的流程；每一步都可追踪和单独重试。

docs.title: F. 微调、量化与推理部署
docs.text:
• 先判断问题是否真的需要微调：知识更新通常先考虑 RAG，格式/风格/行为稳定性才考虑微调。
  • LoRA/QLoRA：理解低秩适配、训练参数量、数据质量、过拟合与模型合并。
  • 量化：区分权重量化与激活量化，比较 FP16/BF16/INT8/INT4 的内存、速度和精度影响。
  • 推理优化：批处理、KV Cache、连续批处理、流式输出、上下文裁剪和缓存。
  • 部署验收：报告吞吐、首 token 延迟、总延迟、峰值显存、单次请求成本和错误率。
  • 版本治理：模型、提示词、索引、数据集和依赖均需有版本；保留回滚路径。

docs.title: G. 视觉、语音与多模态
docs.text:
• 视觉：分类、检测、分割、OCR、图文对齐、视频时序理解。
  • 语音：ASR、TTS、说话人分离、噪声鲁棒性、实时流式处理。
  • 多模态：图像 patch/视觉编码器、跨模态投影、视频帧采样、时间信息和文本对齐。
  • 评估：除总体准确率外，按光照、遮挡、噪声、语言、设备和长尾场景分组。
  • 实践项目：建立小型多模态数据集，记录数据许可、标注规范、错误类型与人工复核结果。

docs.title: H. 端侧 AI 与汽车电子应用
docs.text:
• 部署链路：训练框架 → ONNX/中间表示 → 目标运行时 → NPU/DSP/CPU → 性能与功耗测试。
  • 优化手段：量化、剪枝、蒸馏、算子融合、静态内存规划和输入尺寸控制。
  • 车载场景：驾驶员监测、舱内语音、传感器异常检测、预测性维护；明确安全边界与失效后的降级行为。
  • 工程要求：数据闭环、需求追踪、可复现测试、边界场景覆盖、资源预算和版本回滚。
  • 不应把通用模型输出直接作为安全关键控制指令；需要独立的安全机制、确定性约束与验证。

docs.title: I. AI 安全、隐私与治理
docs.text:
• 幻觉：区分事实错误、推理错误、引用错误和过度自信。
  • 数据风险：个人信息、训练数据许可、机密信息泄露、数据保留和删除机制。
  • 对抗风险：提示注入、工具滥用、数据投毒、模型窃取和越权访问。
  • 公平性：按人群和场景切分评估，检查代表性、错误成本和代理变量。
  • 人机协作：对医疗、法律、财务、安全关键等高风险用途设置专业复核。
  • 上线前检查：威胁建模、红队测试、日志脱敏、访问控制、事故响应与回滚预案。

docs.title: 三、可复现实践项目清单
docs.text: 项目 最小交付物 核心验收指标 经典 ML 分类器 数据清洗脚本、训练脚本、评估报告 与基线对比、无数据泄漏 PyTorch 图像分类 训练/验证代码、模型权重、混淆矩阵 分类别指标、复现实验 个人 Markdown RAG 文档导入、检索、答案引用、删除文档 Recall@k、引用正确率、无答案测试 结构化 LLM 助手 JSON schema、校验、失败重试 结构合规率、任务成功率 工具调用工作流 工具清单、权限、日志、人工确认 工具成功率、超时恢复、安全测试 端侧模型部署 转换脚本、设备测试、资源报告 延迟、内存/显存、功耗、精度差异 AI 评测基准 版本化测试集、自动评分、人工抽检 回归测试覆盖、错误分类与复测

docs.text:
以下链接用于建立长期维护的学习入口；阅读时应优先查看官方文档、版本说明和许可证。

docs.title: 五、专题维护规则
docs.text:
• 每个问题逐步补充：简明答案 → 原理解释 → 最小示例 → 常见误区 → 实践题 → 参考来源。
  • 对变化快的模型、框架和价格标注核查日期与版本；不要把某一时点的模型能力当作永久事实。
  • 资源清单优先保留官方文档、原始论文、维护活跃的代码仓库和可复现实验。
  • 区分“问题已收录”“答案已初稿”“已实验验证”“已复核来源”，不要把问题清单误认为已完成课程。
  • 每个实践项目至少保留 README、依赖版本、运行步骤、测试样本、结果与已知限制。

docs.title: AUTOSAR 1000 问｜原始问题总表
docs.text:
本页由 Flomo 原始总表迁移，保留问题原文与专题分组。答案型子笔记应继续链接到对应问题；此页主要作为问题主干索引。

原始来源： https://v.flomoapp.com/mine/?memo_id=MjMxMTQ2NDk4 创建时间： 2026-04-12T20:40:32+08:00 最近更新： 2026-10-06T21:03:19+08:00 原文长度： 12857 字

答案进度：原始问题总表继续保留，逐题答案分批扩写。第一批已覆盖基础架构、RTE/SW-C、通信栈与网络管理。 - 基础架构与通信栈第一批答案 - 诊断栈、UDS 与 DoIP 工程答案 - NvM、MemIf、Fee 与非易失性存储工程答案 - OS、调度与多核工程答案 - 功能安全、E2E 与信息安全工程答案 - Adaptive AUTOSAR、SOME/IP 与 DDS 工程答案 - CDD、ARXML 自动化与工具链集成工程答案 - 后续继续覆盖诊断、NvM、OS/多核、功能安全、信息安全、Adaptive、工具链与工程排障。

规范笔记库（同步自工作区 AUTOSAR_Module_Notes，R25-11/R26-11 全部 345 篇官方规范）： - AUTOSAR 规范笔记库总索引 — 按平台/类别 345 篇模块笔记，每章含中文标题与正文节选 - 笔记库使用指南 — 笔记库工具链 / AUTOSAR 开发工具链 / 如何读懂 ARXML / RTE 详解 / 网络信号配置操作逻辑

  2. PreCompile、Link、PostBuild 三种变体处理方式——在什么阶段决定用哪个变体？如果一个变体的决策只能在实车上通过诊断指令来切换，选哪种？

E2E / 端到端通信保护深入

  1. E2E Profile 1 到 Profile 7 的区别是什么？Profile 1（CRC+Counter）和 Profile 5（CRC+Counter+Timeout）在实际项目里分别用在什么安全等级的场景？

  2. E2E 保护的报文如果到达了但 CRC 校验失败——接收方 SW-C 应该怎么处理这个数据？直接丢弃还是用上次的有效值？AUTOSAR 有没有推荐的做法？

SW-C 生命周期与状态管理

  1. 一个 Application SW-C 从 ECU 上电到正常运行，它的生命周期是什么？SW-C 在什么时候开始执行 Runnable、什么时候被停止——这些生命周期节点是 SW-C 自身控制的，还是由 EcuM/BswM 等外部模块管理的？

  2. SW-C 可以感知到自身所在的 ECU 正在"唤醒"、"运行"、"休眠"、"关机"吗？如果能，它是通过什么接口收到的？

ARXML 解析与自动化脚本

  1. ARXML 本质上是一个 XML 文件——有没有尝试写脚本（Python + lxml）来自动生成或检查 AUTOSAR 配置？常见的自动化场景有哪些——批量修改 PDU 名称、检查所有 SW-C 端口是否映射完整？

  2. 两个版本的 ARXML 之间做 diff——除了文本层面的差异（XML 行号变了），哪些才是真正影响行为的"语义差异"？怎么在 CI 里自动检测这些差异？

AUTOSAR 与 J1939 集成

  1. 商用车和工程机械常用 J1939（基于 CAN 的上层协议），而乘用车用 AUTOSAR 的 CAN 通信栈——如果把 J1939 的应用层搬到 AUTOSAR 架构上，J1939 的 PGN 和 AUTOSAR 的哪个概念对应？是在 COM 层兼容还是在应用层另写？

  2. J1939 的多帧传输（BAM/CMDT）和 AUTOSAR 的 CanTp 在处理大包传输上的机制有什么不同？如果在一个同时跑 J1939 和 UDS 的 CAN 网络上，两者的传输协议会冲突吗？

AUTOSAR 与 ROS 2 对比

  1. AUTOSAR Adaptive 和 ROS 2 都在用 DDS 做通信中间件——那一个自动驾驶量产的 ECU 能用 ROS 2 代替 AUTOSAR Adaptive 吗？ROS 2 缺了什么（安全、调度确定性、功能安全）？

  2. ROS 2 的"节点"（Node）和 AUTOSAR Adaptive 的"进程"（Process / Execution Cluster）在架构思维上的最大区别是什么？一个 ROS 2 开发者转 AUTOSAR Adaptive，最需要适应的是什么？

工具链自动化构建

  1. 在大项目里，AUTOSAR 配置工具（Davinci / EB）和代码构建（make/cmake）是怎么衔接的？如果每次改配置都要手动点"生成代码"，怎么跟 CI 集成？有没有"命令行无头模式"（headless mode）来做到自动配置生成+编译？

Dcm 协议多路复用（同一诊断栈支持 CAN + DoIP）

  1. 一个 ECU 同时支持 UDS over CAN（通过 CanTp）和 DoIP（通过 DoIP 模块）——Dcm 同时挂两个 Protocol 的配置在工具里怎么做的？诊断请求从 CAN 来和从以太网来，Dcm 怎么区分是同一个服务但不同的传输路径？

  2. 如果用 DoIP 刷写和用 CAN TP 刷写同一个 ECU——两个刷写路径在 Dcm 层的处理逻辑是一样的吗？刷写速率谁快？如果 CAN 路径刷一半断电了，恢复后能接着刷，那 DoIP 路径也支持同样的恢复机制吗？

NvM 块管理策略深入

  1. NvM 的 Block 有 Native 和 Redundant 两种类型——Redundant 存了两份数据，一份坏了还能从另一份恢复。那问题来了：怎么判断"哪一份是好的"？NvM 用什么机制来判断一份数据的完整性？

  2. NvM 的 Write Block 有"立即写"（Immediate）和"周期写"（Periodic）两种策略。如果一个关键参数（如转向角偏移校准值）被 SW-C 改写了，应该用 Immediate 还是 Periodic 来触发 NvM 写？如果用 Periodic，掉电了会不会丢数据？

EcuM 状态机深入（Run / PostRun / Shutdown）

  1. EcuM 的启动序列（Startup Sequence）结束进入 RUN 状态后——哪些 BSW 模块在这个阶段完成了初始化？如果某个 BSW 模块初始化失败，EcuM 会怎么处理——继续启动还是复位？

  2. PostRun 状态是干什么用的？如果所有 SW-C 都停止运行了但 EcuM 还在 PostRun——这期间通常哪些模块还在工作？正在 NvM 写数据的时候收到 Shutdown 请求，EcuM 会强制掉电还是等写完？

CAN 错误处理与 Bus-off 恢复

  1. CAN 控制器进入 Bus-off 状态后，不能再收发任何报文。AUTOSAR 的 Can 驱动和 CanIf 是怎么处理 Bus-off 的？驱动检测到 Bus-off 后，会上报到哪一层来决定什么时候恢复？

  2. Bus-off 恢复策略通常有三种：立即恢复、延迟恢复、手动恢复。在实际项目中（比如动力域 ECU），选哪种策略？如果选了"延迟恢复"，这个延迟是谁来计时——Can 驱动自身的定时器还是 BswM？

AUTOSAR 的数据一致性与 RTE Buffer 管理

  1. 一个 Sender SW-C 以 10ms 的周期写一个 32 位信号，接收方 SW-C 以 20ms 的周期读——如果发送方写到一半数据还没写完就被打断了，接收方读到的是"高字节是新值、低字节是旧值"的拼凑数据吗？RTE 怎么保证这种跨 Runnable 的读/写不被打断？

  2. RTE 的 Buffer 有 queued 和 non-queued 两种模式。queued 模式（队列）能存多条历史数据，non-queued（最后一个）只保留最新值。那如果一个周期 5ms 发送的信号，接收方周期是 100ms——用 queued 还是 non-queued？如果选错了，接收方每次读到的会是什么？

AUTOSAR 启动依赖与 BSW 模块初始化顺序

  1. EcuM 的 Startup Sequence 里注册了多个 BSW 模块的 InitFunction——这些 InitFunction 的执行顺序谁决定的？如果一个模块（比如 Can）依赖另一个模块（比如 IoHwAb 的端口配置），依赖关系在哪声明？

  2. 假设 PduR 的初始化在 CanIf 之前，但 PduR 在初始化时需要知道已经有哪些通信接口（CAN、LIN、FlexRay）可用——那 PduR 先初始化了、CanIf 还没初始化，PduR 怎么知道后面还会有个 CAN 接口加进来？

AUTOSAR 与 Linux 共存（同 SoC 混合部署）

  1. 现在的域控制器和高性能 SoC（如 TDA4、S32G、R-Car）上经常 Linux 跑非实时应用（导航、HMI）、AUTOSAR 跑实时控制（制动、转向）。那 Linux 和 AUTOSAR 之间怎么通信？共享内存？RPMSG？还是走 Ethernet 的 SOME/IP？

  2. 两个 OS 共存的场景下，时间同步问题怎么解决——Linux 那边的 PTP 时间域和 AUTOSAR 的 Global Time 域是同一个吗？如果 Linux 那边 NTP 调整了系统时间，会不会把 AUTOSAR 的调度时间也带偏？
