Request to a Service that is not Offered Status: DRAFT Upstream requirements: , ⌈ When a client requests to read, update, or subscribe to a VSS leaf and the ServiceInterface of the Associated Field / Associated ClientServerOperation is currently not offered, the Automotive API Gateway shall respond with an Error Message with the Error Reason unavailable_data and the associated Error Number and Message according to . ⌋

In this case the Automotive API Gateway shall respond to the client that requested the read with a VISS Error Message with the Error Reason service_unavailable and the associated Error Number and Message according to . ⌋

docs.title: 22. Field Read
docs.text:
Binding of a Field Read Status: DRAFT Upstream requirements: , ⌈ The getting of the value of a Field of a ServiceInterface with VISS deployment shall invoke the registered get handler (see ) of the Field class. The value of the Field shall be the returned value of the get handler. Additional Information:

  • In case a MethodCallProcessingMode of kPoll has been passed to the constructor of the Service Skeleton class (see ), the get handler shall only be executed upon a call to the ProcessNextMethodCall method (see ) of the Service Skeleton class.
  • In case a MethodCallProcessingMode of kEventSingleThread has been passed to the constructor of the Service Skeleton class (see ), the get handler shall only be executed upon completion of all previous calls to get handlers of that Skeleton. ⌋

Note: The specification regarding the MethodCallProcessingMode is similar to , .

docs.title: 23. ClientServerOperation Execution
docs.text:
Binding of a ClientServerOperation Execution Status: DRAFT Upstream requirements: , ⌈ An execution of a ClientServerOperation in the role method of a ServiceInterface with VISS deployment shall correspond to the execution of the service method (see ) that was generated for this ClientServerOperation. The content of the resolved Future returned by the service method shall correspond to the return of the ClientServerOperation. Additional Information:

  • In case a MethodCallProcessingMode of kPoll has been passed to the constructor of the Service Skeleton class (see ), the service method shall only be executed upon a call to the ProcessNextMethodCall method (see ) of the Service Skeleton class.
  • In case a MethodCallProcessingMode of kEventSingleThread has been passed to the constructor of the Service Skeleton class (see ), the service method shall only be executed upon completion of all previous calls to get handlers of that skeleton. ⌋

Note: The return can either be a value or an error.

Note: The specification regarding the MethodCallProcessingMode is similar to , .

docs.title: 24. Subscription
docs.text:
Binding of Field Update Status: DRAFT Upstream requirements: , ⌈ In the context of the Automotive API Gateway an Associated Field shall be considered to receive an update when the Update function according to is called successfully on the respective Field class. ⌋

Note: This will trigger required subscription event messages according to .

Note: This specification is relevant for the programmed solution using a Skeleton. For the declarative approach the update of a field is expressed in relation to the update of a connected field.

docs.text:

Declarative Mapping Status: DRAFT Upstream requirements: ⌈ If a providedInterface of a PPortPrototype of an Automotive API Gateway is referenced by the providedOuterPort of a PassThroughSwConnector the Automotive API Gateway shall behave according to the semantics of that PassThroughSwConnector. ⌋

Note: In future releases closer elaborations are planned to better describe how the modelling can be used to create a declarative mapping to other ServiceInterfaces.

Note: In this situation it might still be desired to generate Skeletons. This is allowed but not mandated by the standard so that implementations of the declarative mapping have full freedom for their implementation.

Network Binding Failure Reaction Status: DRAFT Upstream requirements: ⌈ If during the required interaction with the Service Interfaces due to a VISS request, the Automotive API Gateway receives a ComErrc::kCommunicationFailure it shall reject the VISS request with an Error Message with the Error Reason bad_gateway, the Error Number 502, and the Error Message "The upstream server response was invalid.".

docs.title: 文档简介
docs.text:
This document contains the requirements on the functionality, API and the configuration of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Communication Management as part of the Adaptive AUTOSAR platform foundation.

The Communication Management realizes Service Oriented Communication between Adaptive AUTOSAR Applications for all levels of communication, e.g. IntraProcess, InterProcess, InterMachine. It consists of potentially generated Service Provider Skeletons and Service Requester Proxies and optionally the generic Communication Manager software for central brokering and configuration.

The Communication Management provides a built-in safety mechanism (E2E protection), which can be used for all levels of communication for events and methods.

The documentation of the Communication Management consists of two documents:

  • the ARAComAPI explanatory document , providing explanations of the design and behavior descriptions of the ara::com API,
  • this document, providing the requirements on the ara::com API.

Therefore it is recommended to read the ARAComAPI explanatory document first to get an overview and understanding, and to read this document afterward.

docs.title: 模块依赖
docs.text: This chapter defines the dependencies of this functional cluster to other functional clusters. AUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between functional clusters to allow efficient implementations which might depend e.g., on the used operating system. The goal of this chapter is to provide an informative guideline for the interactions between functional clusters without specifying syntactical details. This ensures compatibility between documents specifying different functional clusters and supports parallel implementation of different functional clusters. Details of internal interfaces are up to the platform provider. Additional internal interfaces, parameters, and return values can be added. A detailed technical architecture documentation of the overall AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform is provided in .

docs.title: 4. 定义 of terms
docs.text:
原文标题：Definition of terms

Term: Description: Callable In the context of C++ a Callable is defined as: A Callable type is a type for which the INVOKE operation (used by, e.g., std::function, std::bind, and std::thread) is applicable. This operation may be performed explicitly using the library function std::invoke. (since C++17) Cycle A cycle describes the time interval of periodical sending and reception of messages. This is important for E2E protected messages with a message counter which shall be increased by the sending entity for every new cycle (= for every new message). Within every cycle the receiving entity shall check if a new message has arrived and if its content is usable. For more information see documents PRS_E2EProtocol (chapter 6) and SWS_E2ELibrary (chapter 9). Event It is a notification mechanism that is used by the Service Skeleton to inform the Service Proxy that a specific condition or state change occurred. The notification includes the data related to the event. Events are sent to a Service Proxy only of it is subscribed to the Event.

docs.title: 28. 总体描述
docs.text:
原文标题：General description

The AUTOSAR Adaptive architecture organizes the software of the AUTOSAR Adaptive foundation as functional clusters. These clusters offer common functionality as services to the applications. The Communication Management (CM) for AUTOSAR Adaptive is such a functional cluster and is part of "AUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive Applications" - ARA. It is responsible for the construction and supervision of communication paths between applications, both local and remote.

The CM provides the infrastructure that enables communication between Adaptive AUTOSAR Applications within one machine and with software entities on other machines, e.g. other Adaptive AUTOSAR applications or Classic AUTOSAR SWCs. All communication paths can be established at design- , start-up- or run-time.

This specification includes the syntax of the API, the relationship of API to the model and describes semantics, e.g. through state machines, and assumption of pre-, post-conditions and use of APIs.

docs.title: 29. Architectural 概念
docs.text:
原文标题：Architectural concepts

The Communication management of AUTOSAR Adaptive can be logically divided into the following sub-parts:

  • Language binding
  • End-to-end communication protection
  • Communication / Network binding
  • Communication Management software

In the context of Communication Management, the following types of interfaces are defined:

  • Public Application Interface: Part of the Adaptive AUTOSAR API and specified in the SWS. This is the standardized ara::com API.
  • Functional Cluster Interactions: Interaction between functional clusters. Not normative, intended to make specification more readable and to support integration of SW into demonstrator. (dotted arrow in ) And also interactions between elements within a functional cluster. Not used in specifications, so it is a non-standardized interface. Used for communication inside Communication Management software (grey arrow in )

Please note, that Language Binding and Communication Binding depend on a specific configuration by the integrator, but they need to be deployed within the application binary. This results in the fact that the serialization of the Communication Binding will run in the execution context of the Adaptive Application.

docs.title: 30. 设计 decisions
docs.text:
原文标题：Design decisions

The design of the ARA API covers the following principles:

  • It uses the Proxy/Skeleton pattern:

  • The (service) proxy is the representative of the possibly remote (i.e. other process, other core, other node) service. It is an instance of a C++ class local to the application/client, which uses the service.

  • The (service) skeleton is the connection of the user provided service implementation to the middleware transport infrastructure. Service implementation class is derived from the (service) skeleton.
  • Beside proxies/skeletons, there might exist a so-called "Runtime" (singleton) class to provide some essentials to manage proxies and skeletons. But this is communication management software implementation specific and therefore not specified in this document, but may be specified in a future version.

Regarding proxy/skeleton design pattern in general and its role in middleware implementations, see . * It supports callback mechanisms on data reception. * The API has zero-copy capabilities including the possibility for memory management in the middleware.

docs.title: 31. Communication paradigms and 定义
docs.text:
原文标题：Communication paradigms and Definitions

Service-Oriented Communication (SoC) as a part of Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) is the main communication pattern for Adaptive AUTOSAR Applications. It allows establishing communication paths both at run-time, so it can be used to build up dynamic communication with unknown number of participants. Figure shows the basic operation principle of Service-Oriented Communication.

Service Discovery decides whether external and internal service-oriented communication is established. The discovery strategy shall allow either returning a specific service instance or all available instances providing the requested service at the time of the request, no matter if they are available locally or remote. The Communication Management software should provide an optimized implementation for both the Service discovery and the communication connection, depending on the location where the service provider resides. More about Service Discovery can be found in SOME/IP Service Discovery Protocol Specification .

The service class is the central element of the Service-Oriented Communication pattern applied in Adaptive AUTOSAR.

docs.title: 32. 服务 contract versioning
docs.text:
原文标题：Service contract versioning

In Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) environments the client and the provider of a service rely on a contract which covers the service interface and behavior. The interface and the behavior of a service may change over time. Therefore, service contract versioning has been introduced to differentiate between the different versions of a service.

The AUTOSAR Adaptive platform supports service contract versioning. The service contract versioning is separated between the design phase and the deployment phase. This means that any service at design level may have its own version number which is mapped to a version number of the used network binding and vice versa. The mapping process is manually done by the service designer or integrator.

Note:

  1. The contract version of a ServiceInterface consists of a majorVersion and a minorVersion number. The majorVersion number indicates backwards-incompatible service changes. The minorVersion number indicates backwards-compatible service changes.

  2. for backwards-incompatible interface or behavior changes the majorVersion number is increased and the minorVersion number is set to 0.

Since the selection of a particular network protocol binding is an integrator driven deployment decision, any change in the selection of a particular network protocol binding or changes in the various attributes and parameters of a particular network protocol binding shall be possible without requiring a re-compilation of the involved adaptive applications. The required changes to the involved adaptive application shall be limited to a re-linking (either static or dynamic) of the involved adaptive application.

docs.title: 34. SOME/IP 网络 binding
docs.text:
原文标题：SOME/IP Network binding

SOME/IP supports different kind of bindings:

SOME/IP Events:

  • unicast is one-to-one communication
  • multi-cast is one-to-many communication

In case the active subscriptions will reach the multi-cast-threshold the communication paradigm will be switched from unicast to multi-cast to gain a better network utilization. Below the multi-cast-threshold SOME/IP is maintaining for a subscription a single unicast communication.

SOME/IP Events:

  • many-to-one communication using multiple unicast communications

The byte order of the SOME/IP header fields is defined as network byte order by .

The byte order of additional fields in the SOME/IP payload is defined as network byte order by .

Payload Byte order definition Upstream requirements: , ⌈ The byte order of the parameters inside the payload shall be defined by byteOrder of ApSomeipTransformationProps. If byteOrder of ApSomeipTransformationProps is not configured explicitly, the default value defined for BYTE_ORDER in shall be used. ⌋

docs.title: 38. FindService message
docs.text:
SOME/IP FindService message Upstream requirements: , , , , , , ⌈ The fields in the SOME/IP FindService message shall be as follows:

  • The Type field and the TTL field shall be set to values suitable for a FindService entry, which means that

  • The Type field shall be set to FindService (see for numerical value)

  • TTL for FindService messages shall not be used, and the value may be set to an arbitrary value. The field is only defined in the protocol for backward compatibility.
  • The Service ID field shall be set to a value derived from the Manifest where the SomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment element defines the serviceInterfaceId.
  • The Instance ID shall be set to a value derived from the Manifest where the RequiredSomeipServiceInstance element defines the requiredServiceInstanceId for the SomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment that is referenced by the RequiredSomeipServiceInstance in the role serviceInterfaceDeployment. If the requiredServiceInstanceId is set to "ALL" then 0xFFFF shall be used.

docs.text:
Sending SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup messages - initial Upstream requirements: , , , , ⌈ The subscription to at least one Event (ServiceInterface.event) of an Eventgroup (SomeipEventGroup) by invoking the Subscribe() method (see ) of the specific Event class of the ServiceProxy class shall cause the sending of a SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup messages in case there is no active subscription for the particular Eventgroup (either because there was no previous subscription to this particular Eventgroup or the TTL of every received SubscribeGroupAck message (see ) for the particular Eventgroup has already expired).

The subscription to at least one Event of an Eventgroup by invoking the Subscribe() method (see ) of the specific Event class of the ServiceProxy class shall not cause the sending of a SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup messages in case there is an active subscription for the particular Eventgroup (because there was some previous subscription to this particular Eventgroup and the TTL of at least one received SubscribeGroupAck message (see ) for the particular Eventgroup has not yet expired). ⌋

docs.title: 文档简介
docs.text: This specification describes the functionality, API and the configuration for the functional cluster Core. To aid in this, it also defines functionality that applies to the entire framework, including a set of common data types used by multiple Functional Clusters as part of their public interfaces.

docs.title: 模块依赖
docs.text:
AUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between Functional Clusters (on platform-level only), to allow efficient implementations, which might depend e.g. on the used Operating System.

This chapter provides an informative guideline of the interaction of Core with other Functional Clusters in the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Section lists the public interfaces provided by Core to other Functional Clusters. Section lists the public interfaces required by Core.

The goal is to provide a clear understanding of Functional Cluster boundaries and interaction, without specifying syntactical details. This ensures compatibility between documents specifying different Functional Clusters and supports parallel implementation of different Functional Clusters. Details of internal interfaces are up to the platform provider. Additional internal interfaces, parameters and return values can be added.

A detailed technical architecture documentation of the overall AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform is provided in .

docs.title: 13. 初始化/De-initialization
docs.text: 原文标题：Initialization/De-initialization

docs.title: 14. Common aspects
docs.text:
This section describes the global initialization and shutdown of the ARA framework. Before the framework is initialized, and after it is de-initialized, not all ARA functionality may be available.

While it is usually possible for a framework implementation to initialize all parts of the framework in an "initialize on first use" fashion, this might not always be desirable, as it introduces potentially noticeable delays during runtime.

For this reason, initialization and shutdown functions exist that may be used by the framework vendor to initialize/shutdown the framework to an extent that no lazy initialization during runtime is necessary.

On the other hand, another framework implementation might well have empty implementations of these functions, e.g. if this framework chooses to fully adopt the "initialize on first use" idiom.

Special ara::core types to be used independently of initialization Upstream requirements: ⌈ A small subset of ara::core types and functions shall be usable independently of initialization with ara::core::Initialize and de-initialization with ara::core::Deinitialize. These are:

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 15. 初始化
docs.text:
原文标题：Initialization

ara::core::Initialize allows a central initialization of all included shared libraries of the ARA framework. This could include initialization of internal data or the setup of daemon links (details are up to the platform vendor).

The general advice for application developers is to call ara::core::Initialize right at the entry point of the application.

Startup and initialization of ARA Upstream requirements: ⌈ The ara::core::Initialize function shall initiate the start-up of the ARA framework, which might include (but is not limited to):

  • initialization of ARA framework specific data structures
  • initialization of system resources
  • spawning of background threads ⌋

Command line argument injection in ara::core::Initialize Upstream requirements: ⌈ If command line argument injection is used in ara::core::Initialize, the relevant command line arguments shall be removed transparently by this function to not influence Application's command line parsing. ⌋

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 16. De-initialization
docs.text:
Shutdown and de-initialization of ARA Upstream requirements: ⌈ The ara::core::Deinitialize function shall initiate the shutdown of the ARA framework, which might include (but is not limited to):

  • orderly shutdown of spawned background threads
  • de-allocation of dynamically allocated memory
  • de-allocation of other system resources ⌋

An error returned by ara::core::Deinitialize is the only way for the ARA to report an error that is guaranteed to be available, e.g. in case ara::log has already been de-initialized. The user is not expected to be able to recover from such an error. However, the user may have a project-specific way of recording errors during de-initialization without ara::log. A typical error case to be reported here is that the user is still holding some resource from the ARA.

Calling ara::core::Deinitialize while ARA APIs are still being called concurrently results in undefined behavior of the application and the framework.

For a proper shutdown, it is also expected that ara::core::Deinitialize is called before the statically initialized data is destructed.

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 17. Sequence of 初始化 and De-initialization
docs.text:
原文标题：Sequence of Initialization and De-initialization

When ara::core::Initialize has returned successfully, calling it again without a prior call to ara::core::Deinitialize will return an error.

When ara::core::Initialize returns with an error, the application may identify the error cause and then try the call again. Calling ara::core::Deinitialize in this case is not necessary, as any necessary cleanup work has already been performed by ara::core::Initialize before returning to the caller.

When ara::core::Deinitialize returns with an error other than kNotInitialized, it is generally unsafe to call either ara::core::Deinitialize or ara::core::Initialize again.

Framework initialization Upstream requirements: ⌈ A successful call of ara::core::Initialize shall bring the framework into a state that makes all its configured components ready for immediate servicing of further API calls. ⌋

Clean deinitialization Upstream requirements: ⌈ A successful call of ara::core::Deinitialize shall bring the framework into a state that is equivalent to the state before the first call to ara::core::Initialize. ⌋

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 18. 错误处理
docs.text:
原文标题：Error handling

During execution of an implementation of Adaptive Platform APIs, different abnormal conditions might be detected and need to be handled and/or reported. Based on their nature, in the following sub-chapters, the types of unsuccessful operations are distinguished within the Adaptive Platform and shall be treated in different ways.

docs.title: 19. ErrorCode
docs.text:
As its name implies, ara::core::ErrorCode is a form of error code; however, it is a class type, loosely modeled on std::error_code, and thus allows much more sophisticated handling of errors than the simple error codes as used in typical C APIs. It always contains a low-level error code value and a reference to an error domain.

The error code value is an enumeration, typically a scoped one. When stored into a ara::core::ErrorCode, it is type-erased into an integral type and thus handled similarly to a C-style error code. The error domain reference defines the context for which the error code value is applicable and thus provides some measure of type safety.

An ara::core::ErrorCode also contains a support data value, which can be defined by an implementation of the Adaptive Platform to give a vendor-specific additional piece of data about the error.

Semantics of ErrorCode Upstream requirements: ⌈ The type ara::core::ErrorCode provides a class interface for storing an error condition. It shall contain these properties:

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 20. 错误 Domain
docs.text:
原文标题：Error Domain

An AUTOSAR ara::core::ErrorDomain is the abstract base class for holding category specific error information in AUTOSAR. This class is loosely based on std::error_category, but differs significantly from it.

An error domain has an associated error code enumeration - ara::core::ErrorDomain::CodeType and an associated base ara::core::Exception type. Both these are usually defined in the same namespace as the ara::core::ErrorDomain sub-class. For normalized access to these associated types, type aliases with standardized names are defined within the ara::core::ErrorDomain sub-class. This makes the ErrorDomain sub-class the root of all data about errors.

Semantics of ErrorDomain Upstream requirements: ⌈ The type ara::core::ErrorDomain defines a context for a set of error conditions. ⌋

docs.title: 21. Usages of ErrorDomain
docs.text:
ErrorDomains may be sub-classed in the following scenarios:

  • functional clusters: AUTOSAR functional clusters or platform extensions APIs are sub-classes of ara::core::ErrorDomain. These are directly standardized by AUTOSAR.
  • applications: AUTOSAR applications may derive ErrorDomains from ApApplicationErrorDomain. These sub-classes of ara::core::ErrorDomain may be generated PortInterface language binding rule
  • implementation-defined: ErrorDomains () / vendor-specific ():

Identity of error domains is defined in terms of unique identifiers. AUTOSAR-defined error domains are given standardized identifiers; user-defined error domains are also required to define unique identifiers.

The ara::core::ErrorDomain class definition requires this unique identifier to be of unsigned 64 bit integer type (std::uint64_t). The range of possible values is large enough to apply UUID-like generation patterns (for UID-64) even if typical UUIDs have 128 bits and are thus larger than that. When a new error domain is created (either an AUTOSAR defined or an user defined one) an according Id shall be randomly generated, which represents this error domain.

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 22. 错误 domain Identifiers
docs.text:
原文标题：Error domain Identifiers

Each error domain has a numeric identifier that is used to determine equality of error domains. The error domains that are pre-defined by the Adaptive Platform have standardized identifiers. Application-specific error domains should make sure their identifiers are system-wide unique.

The full range of unique error domain identifiers is partitioned into a range of:

  • AUTOSAR-standardized Ids: MSB=1; reserved by AUTOSAR; shown in
  • Vendor-specific Ids: MSB=1; reserved by an AUTOSAR stack vendor
  • User-defined Ids: MSB=0; defined via ApApplicationErrorDomain.value

Regardless of the origin of an error domain identifier, it shall be unique in the platform.

Error domain identifier Upstream requirements: ⌈ All sub-classes of error domains specified in the standard shall implement the ErrorDomain::Id() function which shall return the system wide unique error domain identifier of the ara::core::ErrorDomain from . ⌋

AUTOSAR error domain range Upstream requirements: ⌈ Error domain identifiers where bit #63 is set to 1 and bit #62 is set to 0 are reserved for AUTOSAR-defined error domains. ⌋

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 23. Vendor 错误 domains
docs.text:
原文标题：Vendor error domains

Each API that specifies a return type capable of holding an instance of ara::core::ErrorCode typically specifies a number of specified errors. These are error conditions that all or at least most implementations of that API are expected to generate.

In addition to that, however, an implementation may also return additional, non-specified errors. These are called vendor-specific errors.

Note: This applies in particular to APIs returning ara::core::Result or ara::core::Future.

Vendor-specific errors Upstream requirements: ⌈ A vendor-specific error shall use a vendor-specific error domain. ⌋

docs.title: 24. Creating new 错误 domains
docs.text:
原文标题：Creating new error domains

Any new software module with significant logical separation from all existing modules of the Adaptive Platform should define one or more own error domains.

An error domain consists of:

  • an error condition enumeration
  • an exception base class
  • an ara::core::ErrorDomain sub-class
  • a non-member ErrorDomain sub-class accessor function
  • a non-member MakeErrorCode function overload

All these are to reside not in the ara::core namespace, but in the "target" one.

Custom error domain scope Upstream requirements: ⌈ The ara::core::ErrorDomain sub-class and the corresponding enumeration, exception base class, non-member accessor function, and the MakeErrorCode overload shall be defined in the same namespace as the software module for which they are being specified. ⌋

Note: This is to help making sure that the C++ ADL mechanism works as expected by other parts of this standard.

An error domain defined in the way specified in this section is suitable to be used for the ApApplicationErrorDomain model element.

Throughout this section, the character sequence is a placeholder for the shortname of the ApApplicationErrorDomain.

docs.title: 25. ErrorDomain sub-class
docs.text:
Then, a new class is created that derives from ara::core::ErrorDomain and overrides all the pure virtual member functions. In addition to that, it also needs to define in its scope a type alias called Errc for the error condition enumeration, as well as another type alias called Exception for the exception base class for this new error domain.

ErrorDomain sub-class type Upstream requirements: ⌈ Each error domain shall define a class type that derives publicly from ara::core::ErrorDomain. ⌋

ErrorDomain sub-class naming Upstream requirements: ⌈ All sub-classes of ara::core::ErrorDomain shall follow the naming scheme ErrorDomain, where is the shortname of the ApApplicationErrorDomain. ⌋

Error domain message Upstream requirements: ⌈ All sub-classes of ara::core::ErrorDomain shall implement the ErrorDomain::Message() function, which shall return the description text, for any given error code in its domain. ⌋

ErrorDomain sub-class non-extensibility Upstream requirements: , ⌈ All sub-classes of ara::core::ErrorDomain shall be final. ⌋

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 26. Non-member ErrorDomain sub-class accessor 功能
docs.text:
原文标题：Non-member ErrorDomain sub-class accessor function

A non-member accessor function for the new error domain class is to be defined. For an error domain class MyErrorDomain, the accessor function is named GetMyErrorDomain. This accessor function returns a reference to a single global instance of that class. This accessor function shall be fully constexpr-capable; this in turn implies that the ErrorDomain sub-class also shall be constexpr-constructible (see ).

ErrorDomain sub-class accessor function Upstream requirements: ⌈ For all sub-classes of ara::core::ErrorDomain, there shall be a non-member constexpr function that returns a reference-to-const to a singleton instance of it. ⌋

ErrorDomain sub-class accessor function naming Upstream requirements: ⌈ All ara::core::ErrorDomain sub-class accessor functions shall follow the naming scheme GetErrorDomain, where is the shortname of the ApApplicationErrorDomain. ⌋

ErrorDomain sub-class accessor function Upstream requirements: ⌈ All ara::core::ErrorDomain sub-class accessor functions shall have a return type of const ErrorDomain&. ⌋

docs.title: 27. Non-member MakeErrorCode overload
docs.text:
A non-member factory function MakeErrorCode needs to be defined, which is implicitly used by the convenience constructors of class ara::core::ErrorCode. This factory function will make use of the non-member accessor function for the error domain sub-class, and call the type-erased constructor of class ara::core::ErrorCode.

MakeErrorCode overload for new error domains Upstream requirements: ⌈ For all sub-classes of ara::core::ErrorDomain, there shall be a constexpr overload of the non-member function MakeErrorCode that creates an ara::core::ErrorCode instance for a given error condition value within the ara::core::ErrorDomain sub-class's error condition range. ⌋

MakeErrorCode overload signature Upstream requirements: ⌈ All overloads of the non-member function MakeErrorCode shall have the following signature:

constexpr ErrorCode MakeErrorCode(Errc code, ErrorDomain::SupportDataType data) noexcept;

where is the shortname of the ApApplicationErrorDomain. ⌋

docs.title: 28. 错误 condition enumeration
docs.text:
原文标题：Error condition enumeration

The error condition enumeration describes all known error conditions of the new software module. It should be reasonably fine-grained to allow users to differentiate error conditions that they might want to handle in different ways.

Error condition enumeration type Upstream requirements: ⌈ Each error domain shall define an error condition enum class with the base type ara::core::ErrorDomain::CodeType that holds all error conditions of that error domain. ⌋

Error condition enumeration naming Upstream requirements: ⌈ Error domain error condition enumerations shall follow the naming scheme Errc, where is the shortname of the ApApplicationErrorDomain. ⌋

Error condition enumeration contents Upstream requirements: ⌈ Error domain error condition enumerations shall not contain any values that indicate success. ⌋

Error condition enumeration numbers Upstream requirements: ⌈ Error domain error condition enumerations shall keep the number 0 unassigned. ⌋

docs.title: 29. Exception base class
docs.text:
As a complement to the error condition enumeration, an exception base class for this error domain also needs to be defined. This exception base class is used for the "transformation" of an ara::core::ErrorCode object into an exception.

Additional exception types can be defined by the software module, but all these then derive from this base type.

ErrorDomain exception base type Upstream requirements: ⌈ Each error domain shall define an exception base type that is a sub-class of ara::core::Exception. ⌋

ErrorDomain exception base type naming Upstream requirements: ⌈ All error domain exception base types specified by shall follow the naming scheme Exception, where is the shortname of the ApApplicationErrorDomain. ⌋

ErrorDomain exception type hierarchy Upstream requirements: ⌈ All additional exception types defined by a software module shall have the exception base type specified by as a base class. ⌋

docs.title: 30. 错误 Domain C++ pseudo 代码示例
docs.text:
原文标题：Error Domain C++ pseudo code example

The following C++ pseudo code illustrates how these definitions come together:

namespace my {

enum class Errc : ara::core::ErrorDomain::CodeType { // ... };

class Exception : public ara::core::Exception { public: Exception(ara::core::ErrorCode err) noexcept; };

class ErrorDomain final : public ara::core::ErrorDomain { public: using Errc = Errc; using Exception = Exception; 

constexpr <SN>ErrorDomain() noexcept;

const char* Name() const noexcept override;
const char* Message(ara::core::ErrorDomain::CodeType errorCode) const noexcept override;
void ThrowAsException(const ara::core::ErrorCode& errorCode) const noexcept(false) override;

};

constexpr const ara::core::ErrorDomain& GetErrorDomain() noexcept;

constexpr ara::core::ErrorCode MakeErrorCode(Errc code, ara::core::ErrorDomain::SupportDataType data) noexcept;

} // namespace my

docs.title: 31. Result
docs.text:
The ara::core::Result type follows the ValueOrError concept from the C++ proposal p0786 . It either contains a value (of type ValueType), or an error (of type ErrorType). Both ValueType and ErrorType are template parameters of ara::core::Result, and due to their templated nature, both value and error can be of any type. ErrorType is defaulted to ara::core::ErrorCode, and it is enforced that only this type is allowed as the ErrorType template parameter for ara::core::Result.

ara::core::Result acts as a "wrapper type" that connects the exception-less API approach using ara::core::ErrorCode with C++ exceptions. As there is a direct mapping between ara::core::ErrorCode and a domain-specific exception type, ara::core::Result allows to "transform" its embedded ara::core::ErrorCode into the appropriate exception type, by calling ara::core::Result::ValueOrThrow.

Semantics of ara::core::Result Upstream requirements: , , ⌈ The type ara::core::Result shall provide a means to handle both return values and errors from synchronous function calls in an exception-less way, by providing an encapsulated return type which may be either:

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 32. Future and Promise
docs.text:
ara::core::Future and its companion class ara::core::Promise are closely modeled on std::future and std::promise, but have been adapted to interoperate with ara::core::Result. Similar to ara::core::Result described in section , the class ara::core::Future either contains a value, or an error (the Future first has to be in "ready" state, though).

Class ara::core::Promise has been adapted in two aspects:

  • std::promise::set_exception has been removed and ara::core::Promise::SetError has been introduced in its stead.
  • For ara::core::Future, there is a new member function ara::core::Future::GetResult that is similar to ara::core::Future::get, but never throws an exception and returns a ara::core::Result instead.

Thus, ara::core::Future as return type allows the same dual approach to error handling as ara::core::Result, in that it either works exception-based (with ara::core::Future::get), or exception-free (with ara::core::Future::GetResult).

ara::core::Result is a type used for returning values or errors from a synchronous function call, whereas ara::core::Future is a type used for returning values or errors from an asynchronous function call.

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 33. Exceptions
docs.text:
The Adaptive Platform defines a base exception type ara::core::Exception for all exceptions defined in the standard. This exception takes a ara::core::ErrorCode object as mandatory constructor argument, similar to the way std::system_error takes a std::error_code argument for construction.

Below this exception base type, there is an additional layer of exception base types, one for each error domain.

For error domains that are modeled in ARXML, the C++ language binding will generate an exception class in addition to the ErrorDomain sub-class (which is described in section ). This exception class also conforms to a standard naming scheme: shortName of ApApplicationErrorDomain plus Exception suffix (this makes it distinguishable from the ara::core::ErrorDomain sub-class itself). It is located in the same namespace as the corresponding ara::core::ErrorDomain sub-class.

docs.title: 34. Duality of ErrorCode and Exception
docs.text:
By using the classes listed above, all APIs of the Adaptive Platform can be used with either an exception-based or an exception-less error handling workflow. However, no API function will ever treat an Error by throwing an exception directly; it will always return an error code in the form of a ara::core::Result or ara::core::Future return value instead. It is then possible for the caller to "transform" the Error into an exception, typically via the member function ara::core::Result::ValueOrThrow.

When working with a C++ compiler that does not support exceptions at all (or one that has been configured to disable them with an option such as g++'s -fno-exceptions), all API functions still show the same behavior. What does differ then is that ara::core::Result::ValueOrThrow is not defined - this member function is only defined when the compiler does support exceptions.

docs.title: 35. Explicitly aborting an Operation
docs.text:
If a Violation has been detected by the implementation of an API function, mandates to abort this operation immediately. It allows two ways to do this; either by throwing certain kinds of exceptions (if the implementation supports C++ exceptions), or by calling ara::core::Abort.

Calling ara::core::Abort will result in an Explicitly aborting an Operation, which usually leads to an Abnormal Termination as defined by . This section defines the behavior of this mechanism.

Like std::abort, calling ara::core::Abort is meant to terminate the current process abnormally and immediately, without performing stack unwinding and without calling destructors of static objects.

Standard Error Stream Logging of Explicitly aborting an Operation Upstream requirements: ⌈ Calling ara::core::Abort shall result in a log message being output to the process' standard error stream. The log message shall contain the string representation of the parameters that have been passed to the function as arguments, in the same order that they have been passed. ⌋

docs.title: 文档简介
docs.text:
This specification describes the functionality and the configuration for the Adaptive AUTOSAR Functional Cluster Cryptography (FC Crypto) and its API (CryptoAPI, which is part of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform Foundation.

The FC Crypto offers applications and other Adaptive AUTOSAR Functional Clusters a standardized interface for operations including cryptographic operations, key management, and certificate handling. FC Crypto manages the actual implementations of all operations, the configuration, and the brokering of operations from applications to implementations. The standardized interface is exposed by the CryptoAPI.

docs.title: 7. Assumptions on the Implementation of Crypto
8. Process Isolation
docs.text: In order to perform access control on keys and certificates, the implementation of Crypto must not be limited to the application process, i.e., it is assumed that it is not executed as a library-only implementation. Instead, the implementation of Crypto may relay on separate processes or other forms of trust boundaries (e.g., trusted execution environments).

docs.title: 15. 功能规范
docs.text:
原文标题：Functional specification

The AUTOSAR Adaptive architecture organizes the software of the AUTOSAR Adaptive foundation as Functional Clusters. These clusters offer common functionality as services to the applications. The Functional Cluster Cryptography (FC Crypto) is part of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform Foundation.

The FC Crypto provides the infrastructure to access multiple implementations of cryptographic operations through a standardized interface. It provides access to cryptographic primitives via the Crypto Provider and access to certificate management via the X.509 Certificate Management Provider. It supports common automotive security use-cases like secure communication (e.g., SecOC, TLS), authenticated diagnostics (e.g, service 0x29), and secure software update.

This specification includes the syntax and functional behavior of the API and its relationship to the model.

docs.title: 16. 架构 & 概念
docs.text:
原文标题：Architecture & Concepts

In this section the architecture of Crypto and several concepts used by Crypto are described.

docs.title: 17. 架构
docs.text:
原文标题：Architecture

The FC Crypto offers applications and other Adaptive AUTOSAR Functional Clusters a standardized interface to perform cryptographic operations, manage cryptographic keys, and handle certificate. The interfaces defined by FC Crypto are designed to enable integraton of 3rd party cryptographic libraries and hardware-based elements (e.g., HSMs). This facilitates implementation of a security "trust anchor" or acceleration of cryptographic transformations.

Figure depicts the high-level architecture of FC Crypto.

A CryptoProvider provides access to the implementation of a set of cryptographic primitives and a key storage. Typically, an cryptographic module within a trusted execution environment is providing the actual implementation of primitives and key storage, and the CryptoProvider is providing a wrapper that allows access to different implementations using the same interface. A CryptoProvider is implemented by a stack vendor or a third party by implementing the ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider class, as well as the classes for cryptographic contexts and the classes for cryptographic keys. It is possible to have multiple different CryptoProviders instantiated on one machine.

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 19. Usage of Crypto by Applications
docs.text:
This section describes the required modelling during the design and deployment phase of an adaptive application. During design, the application designer has to decide, which persisted cryptographic keys, which persisted certificates, and which CryptoProviders the application will use.

  • For each persisted key that will be used and modified by an application (e.g., the key is generated by the application and later used for signature generation), the application designer creates a CryptoKeySlotInterface.
  • For each persisted key that will be used by an application, but modified only by a different application, the application designer creates a CryptoKeySlotClientInterface.
  • For each persisted certificate that will be used by an application, the application designer creates a CryptoCertificateInterface.
  • For each group of persisted certificates that will be used by an application, the application designer creates a CryptoCertificateGroupInterface.
  • For each CryptoProvider that will be used by an application independently of cryptographic keys (e.g., to calculate cryptographic hash values), the application designer creates a CryptoProviderInterface.

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 20. Usage of Crypto by other 功能性 Clusters
docs.text:
原文标题：Usage of Crypto by other Functional Clusters

The implementation of some Adaptive Platform Services such as update and configuration, communication, persistency, or diagnostics also require access to cryptographic services and cryptographic keys to fulfill their functionality. Such access is modelled using cross functional cluster mappings. For instance, if a key is being used by SecOC for protection of a PDU, the model element ComSecOcToCryptoKeySlotMapping is used to configure the KeySlot to be used by SecOC. A detailled description of the available model can be found in the TPS Manifest in Chapter Cross-functional cluster interaction.

Typically, such key material is only used by a functional cluster, but managed (e.g., imported, generated, updated) by an adaptive application. In this case, the mechanisms described in Section are used.

docs.title: 21. Access 控制
docs.text:
原文标题：Access Control

Crypto supports implementing the least privilege principle by restricting, which application can use and modify cryptographic keys and certificates. The policy, i.e., which application can access which resource in which way, is modelled in the manifest and enforced at runtime. In order to enforce these access restrictions, a separation between the application process using ara::crypto and the policy enforcement is required. This separation can be implemented using, e.g., OS mechanisms such as process isolation.

Access to a KeySlot is limited to certain processes in the manifest using the CryptoKeySlotPortMapping (see ) and CryptoKeySlotClientPortMapping (see ) model elements:

Access Control on Loading KeySlots Upstream requirements: , ⌈ Crypto shall restrict the processes that can load the content of a CryptoKeySlot to those Processes that are referenced by either

  • a CryptoKeySlotPortMapping or
  • aCryptoKeySlotClientPortMapping

that are aggregated by the respective CryptoKeySlot and which also reference the Process via either

  • a CryptoKeySlotPortMapping.CryptoProcessRef or
  • a CryptoKeySlotClientPortMapping.CryptoProcessRef.

docs.title: 22. Usage 控制
docs.text:
原文标题：Usage Control

When a key is generated, imported, or derived, the application can limit how the key can be used afterwards. The type ara::crypto::AllowedUsageFlags is used to represent the allowed usages of a key as a bitmask. Table gives an overview of the available allowed usages. Multiple flags can be combined with a bitwise or in order to allow several usages of a key.

Allowed Usage Flag Applicable Key Type Description Relevant Contexts/Functions kAllowDataEncryption SymmetricKey, PublicKey The key can be used for data encryption SymmetricCipherCtx, AuthCipherCtx, EncryptorPublicCtx kAllowDataDecryption SymmetricKey, PrivateKey The key can be used for data decryption. SymmetricCipherCtx, AuthCipherCtx, DecryptorPrivateCtx kAllowMac SymmetricKey The key can be used for MAC generation and verification. MessageAuthnCodeCtx kAllowSigGeneration PrivateKey The key can be used for signature generation. SignerPrivateCtx kAllowSigVerification PublicKey The key can be used for signature verification. VerifierPublicCtx kAllowKeyAgreement PrivateKey, PublicKey The key can be used as private or public input to key agreement.

docs.title: 23. Identification of Cryptographic Transformations and Key 类型
docs.text:
原文标题：Identification of Cryptographic Transformations and Key Types

The type of all keys and cryptographic transformations must be unambiguously identifiable to enable the application designer and developer to unambiguously express the desired key types and transformations to by used by the CryptoProvider.

The type of a key is typically defined by an algorithm (e.g., AES, RSA, ed25519) and optionally by a length (e.g., 2048 bit) or curve (e.g., secp256r1), and whether the key is a private or public key. A cryptographic transformation is typically defined by several elements:

  • The operation that is performed by the transformation, e.g., hashing, encryption, signature verification.
  • The algorithm that forms the basis of the transformation, e.g., SHA2-256, AES-128, ed25519.
  • An optional variant that specifies how the algorithm is applied. This includes the mode (e.g., CBC), the signature scheme (e.g., RSAES-OAEP), the used curve (e.g., secp256r1), and the number of rounds.
  • An optional parameter that specifies, e.g., an additional algorithm that is executed as part of the transformation (e.g., SHA2-256, Poly1305) or padding (e.g., PKCS7).

docs.title: 24. Concurrent Access
docs.text:
While unlimited concurrent access to ara::crypto is theoreticaly possible, in reality there are only limited resources available. For instance, an HSM might only have a certain number of AES accelerators, limiting the number of operations that can be processed in parallel. In order to represent this behavior, all functions of ara::crypto, which may need to allocate resources, may return kBusyResource in case the requested operation temporarly cannot be performed because a required resource is busy. This includes all functions for key generation, loading keys, importing keys, the Start() function of transformation contexts' streaming interface, and the single-call functions of transformation contexts.

Limit concurrent access to internal resources Upstream requirements: ⌈ All functions of ara::crypto shall return kBusyResource if the requested operation temporarly cannot be performed because a required resource is busy. ⌋

The implementation of a CryptoProvider may perform internal scheduling or sequentializing of operations.

docs.title: 25. 功能性 Cluster Lifecycle
docs.text: 原文标题：Functional Cluster Lifecycle

docs.title: 26. 启动
docs.text:
原文标题：Startup

Using ara::core::Initialize and ara::core::Deinitialize, the application can initialize and de-initialize FC Crypto resources allocated to the application.

Upstream requirements: ⌈ When ara::core::Initialize is called, the FC Crypto shall read in the manifest information and prepare the access structures that are defined in the manifest. ⌋

Hint: Access structures may encompass the communication channel between the application process and the stack process or other resource required by the CryptoAPI.

Log initialization failed Upstream requirements: ⌈ Whenever Initialization of crypto structures failed during a call of ara::core::Initialize, FC Crypto shall log a DltMessage of type InitializationFailed with arguments set to:

  • ProcessId: The process failed to initialize crypto ⌋

docs.title: 27. 关机
docs.text:
原文标题：Shutdown

Upstream requirements: , , ⌈ When ara::core::Deinitialize is called, the FC Crypto shall ensure that all open contexts are closed and all occupied ressources are freed. ⌋

Upstream requirements: ⌈ When ara::core::Deinitialize is called, the FC Crypto shall ensure that all associated persist operations in this context of this application are executed successfully and no new persist operations are started. ⌋

Log deInitialization failed Upstream requirements: ⌈ Whenever deInitialization of crypto structures failed during call of ara::core::Deinitialize, FC Crypto shall log a DltMessage of type DeInitializationFailed with arguments set to:

  • ProcessId: The process failed to deInitialize crypto ⌋

Note: the application is expected not to call any API of FC Crypto before ara::core::Initialize or after ara::core::Deinitialize. According to SWS_CORE_90021, such behavior will be trated as a violation.

Initialization violation Upstream requirements: ⌈ The function ara::crypto::LoadX509Provider shall check that ara::core::Initialize has been called successfully and ara::core::Deinitialize has not yet been executed.

docs.title: 28. Crypto Provider
docs.text:
A Crypto Provider is a structural element that organizes Cryptographic primitives. Every Crypto Provider typically represents either one hardware element, e.g., trusted platform module (TPM) or hardware security module (HSM), or one software element, e.g., cryptographic library.

Functionality of a CryptoProvider Upstream requirements: ⌈ Each derived implementation of the interface class ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider shall encapsulate cryptographic transformations and associated resources, such as ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoObject and Cryptographic primitives, of a single software or hardware cryptography implementation. ⌋

Note: a Crypto Provider may expose only a subset of all available transformations or primitives of the underlying software or hardware cryptography implementation (e.g. in case of weak or outdated primitives). However, this implementation detail shall be documented and communicated to the user.

Upstream requirements: , ⌈ Derived implementations of the interface class ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider shall isolate all non-session Key Material from the user (Adaptive Application). ⌋

docs.title: 29. KeySlot Access
docs.text:
An application can use the InstanceSpecifier representing a modeled CryptoKeySlotInterface or CryptoKeySlotClientInterface to access a KeySlot. If a CryptoKeySlotClientInterface is used, the key stored in the KeySlot can only be used but not modified. Usage of a CryptoKeySlotInterface additionally allows modification of the key stored in the KeySlot. The container CryptoKeySlotPortMapping associates the enclosing CryptoKeySlot with a Process, and an RPortPrototype.

If a KeySlot is only accessed in a read-only manner, the function ara::crypto::LoadKeySlot can be used to get a KeySlot object that is read-only.

LoadKeySlot Upstream requirements: ⌈ The function ara::crypto::LoadKeySlot shall return the KeySlot instance that represents the key slot resource identified by the provided ara::core::InstanceSpecifier representing a modeled CryptoKeySlotInterface or CryptoKeySlotClientInterface through the CryptoKeySlotPortMapping. ⌋

If a KeySlot will also be modified, the function ara::crypto::LoadWriteableKeySlot can be used to get a WriteableKeySlot object, which can be used to modify the content of the KeySlot.

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 30. CryptoProvider Instantiation
docs.text:
Crypto provides two functions to instantiate a CryptoProvider. First, if a CryptoProviderInterface is modelled, the function ara::crypto::LoadCryptoProvider can be used to instantiate a CryptoProvider. The main use cases for such a direct instantiation are, e.g., the use of keyless operations such as hashing or the generation and use of session keys. Secondly, if the application accesses modelled KeySlots as described in Section , the function ara::crypto::cryp::KeySlot::GetCryptoProvider can be used to instantiate the correct CryptoProvider for subsequent use of the stored key.

Log Crypto Provider loading failed Upstream requirements: ⌈ Whenever Loading a Crypto Provider failed when calling ara::crypto::LoadCryptoProvider, FC Crypto shall log a DltMessage of type CryptoProviderLoadingFailed with arguments set to:

  • CryptoProviderInstanceSpecifier: Crypto Provider instance specifier. ⌋

docs.title: 31. Runtime Key Instantiation and Usage
docs.text:
After loading a KeySlot, the KeySlot object can either be loaded into a CryptoProvider in order to obtain a runtime CryptoObject, or it can be used directly in a transformation context in order to specify the key used for the cryptographic transformation (cf. ).

A runtime key object can be creating using the functions ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::LoadSymmetricKey, ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::LoadPublicKey, and ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::LoadPrivateKey.

A runtime key can be stored in a KeySlot that is managed by the same CryptoProvider and has the same AlgId and CryptoObjectType as the runtime key using the function ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoObject::Save.

Save runtime key to a KeySlot Upstream requirements: ⌈ The function ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoObject::Save shall verify that the AllowedUsageFlags include kAllowPersist, verify that the KeySlot is compatible to the key, verify that the KeySlot is writeable by the application, verify that the key currently stored in the KeySlot is not being used in an ongoing streaming operation, and store the key represented by the CryptoObject in the provided KeySlot. ⌋

Note: Write access to a KeySlot is defined in .

docs.title: 32. Utility functions
docs.text: The classes ara::crypto::cryp::SymmetricKey, ara::crypto::cryp::PublicKey, and ara::crypto::cryp::PrivateKey provide the function ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoObject::GetAlgId to query the AlgId of the key. The classes ara::crypto::cryp::SymmetricKey, ara::crypto::cryp::PublicKey, and ara::crypto::cryp::PrivateKey provide the function ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoObject::GetAllowedUsage to query the AllowedUsage (cf. ) of the key. A ara::crypto::cryp::PrivateKey provides the function ara::crypto::cryp::PrivateKey::GetPublicKey that allows to query the corresponding public key.

docs.title: 33. Key Generation
docs.text:
In order to generate new keys, a CryptoProvider provides the functions ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::GenerateSymmetricKey and ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::GeneratePrivateKey. An application can pass a AlgId identifying the type of the key and the allowed usages of the generated key to the functions.

Upstream requirements: ⌈ The functions ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::GeneratePrivateKey and ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::GenerateSymmetricKey shall generate secret key-material according to the provided ara::crypto::AlgId and return an instance of ara::crypto::cryp::PrivateKey or ara::crypto::cryp::SymmetricKey, respectively. Each function shall initialize the object according to the provided ara::crypto::AllowedUsageFlags. ⌋

docs.title: 34. Plaintext Key 管理
docs.text: 原文标题：Plaintext Key Management

docs.title: 35. Plaintext Key Import
docs.text:
Key material can be imported into a CryptoProvider in plaintext form and in protected form. The functions ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::ImportPublicKey, ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::ImportSymmetricKey , and ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::ImportPrivateKey can be used to import plaintext key material. When importing a key, the application can set the allowed usage of the imported key.

Depending on the key material and the context, importing or exporting confidential plaintext key material may represent a security risk. Therefore, the use of plaintext key import or export should be evaluated carefully by all involved parties. Additionally, a CryptoProvider may not support plaintext import or export of certain key types (e.g., symmetric or private keys) for security reasons.

Import of public keys Upstream requirements: ⌈ The function ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::ImportPublicKey shall deserialize the provided serialized data from the format specified using the formatId parameter.

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 36. Plaintext Key Export
docs.text:
The function ara::crypto::Serializable::ExportPublicly provides a way to export symmetric, private, and public keys.

Exporting public objects Upstream requirements: ⌈ The function ara::crypto::Serializable::ExportPublicly shall serialize the object in the format specified using the formatId parameter, write the serialized data into the provided output data buffer, and return the size of the written serialized data. If the function is a member function of a PublicKey, PrivateKey, or SymmetricKey, it shall additionally verify prior to serialization that its allowed usage includes kAllowPlaintextExport and the parameter CryptoKeySloyPortMapping.AllowPlainTextExport of the CryptoKeySlotPortMapping from which the object was loaded is configured as True. ⌋

docs.title: 37. Protected Key 管理
docs.text: 原文标题：Protected Key Management

docs.title: 38. Protected Key Import
docs.text:
Key material can be imported into a CryptoProvider in protected form including associated meta-data such as allowed-usage. This combination of key-material and meta-data is typically generated in a trusted environment of the OEM or another authorized entity.

These update packages fall into two categories: OEM custom packages and standardized packages specified for example by SHE (e.g. as used by command SHE/LOADKEY).

FC Crypto supports both categories by specifying the ProtectedKeyImportCtx. As with other contexts the ProtectedKeyImportCtx allows a CryptoProvider to be tailored to easily fulfill project requirements. Creating a ProtectedKeyImportCtx using the string-based ara::crypto::AlgId the application developer can selected the import protocol required for his project and supported by the chosen CryptoProvider.

One example, as already mentioned above, is the data format specified in AUTOSAR_TR_SecureHardwareExtensions. A package compatible with the command SHE/LOADKEY includes a header specifying the key-slot to update and the key-slot, whose content shall be used for unwrapping the protected payload (key-encryption-key or KEK).

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 39. Protected Key Export
docs.text: Protected key exporting is supported by ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoProvider::ExportSecuredKey. Similar in usage to the ProtectedKeyImportCtx it allows to specify the AlgId to be used (i.e. the protocol specifying the protection wrapper and structure of the protected payload) as well as optionally the KEK, if not implicitly specified with the AlgId. This interface is offered by the CryptoProvider directly as a dedicated context would just replicate interfaces already offered by the ara::crypto::cryp::CryptoObject to be exported.

docs.title: 40. Import and Export Formats
docs.text:
The ara::crypto::FormatId is used to define data formats and encodings for importing and exporting data to and from ara::crypto.

Raw Format Upstream requirements: ⌈ If a function accepts a ara::crypto::FormatId and the ara::crypto::FormatId is set to kFormatRawValueOnly, then the function shall (de-)serialize the object in the following formats depending on the object's type:

  • SymmetricKey: The serialized, raw value of the symmetric key. | * ed25519/ed448 signature: R | S (RFC 8032). | |---|---| | * ECDSA signature: R | S (IEEE P1363). |

  • RSA PSS signature: S (RFC 8017).

  • RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature: S (RFC 8017). | * SLH-DSA signature: R | SIG_FORS | SIG_HT (IETF draft-ietf-lamps-cms-sphincs-plus) | |---|---|---|

⌋

DER Format Upstream requirements: ⌈ If a function accepts a ara::crypto::FormatId and the ara::crypto::FormatId is set to kFormatDerEncoded, then the function shall (de-)serialize the object in DER (X.690) according to the following schema depending on the object's type:

  • Public Key: SubjectPublicKeyInfo (RFC 5280)
  • Private Key: OneAsymmetricKey (RFC 5958)
  • Signature: signatureValue (RFC 5280) ⌋

docs.title: 文档简介
docs.text:
This document describes common aspects of usage of Adaptive Platform functionality towards Base SW, such as the OS or other kinds of "lower layer" SW. For the latter this may include requirements, proposed default settings of configuration parameters, usage constraints and alike. The previously used term 'common' indicates that the usage aspects do not reflect a single functional cluster (FC) perspective but instead addresses Base SW considerations potentially used by several functional clusters. In contrast Base SW aspects related to individual FC usage are covered by the respective SWS documents.

This document's main purpose is to assist different roles for setting up an development AP project such as the integrator. As such the Base SW topics in this document are not necessarily connected on their technical subjects. The focus of the document shall not be mixed with , the latter addresses the interface from Adaptive Application perspective.

In contrast to many other AUTOSAR software specifications, this document is not related to a specific SW component (such as AP functional cluster).

docs.title: 18. 可信平台
docs.text:
原文标题：Trusted Platform

From a security perspective, it is essential that all software executed on the Adaptive Platform is trusted, i.e. the integrity and authenticity of the software is ensured.

A key requirement for a trusted Adaptive Platform is a Trust Anchor on the Machine that is authentic by definition (hence that alternative name, "root of trust"). A Trust Anchor is often realized as a public key stored in a secure environment, e.g. in non-modifiable persistent memory or in an HSM. The trust has to be extended to the Machine by appropriate means, e.g. by a chain of trust. If the Machine does not exhibit a Trust Anchor, it cannot be ensured that the Adaptive Platform is trusted.

Availability of a Trust Anchor ⌈ If there is no Trust Anchor available on the Machine, the following requirements may be ignored: , , , , , , , , , . ⌋

There are many ways to verify the integrity and authenticity of the Adaptive Platform. A Trusted Platform can be realized e.g. (but not limited to) by

  • Verification of the complete Ramdisk by the Bootloader
  • Verification of individual Executables and data files, e.g.

docs.title: 19. 处理 of failed authenticity checks
docs.text:
原文标题：Handling of failed authenticity checks

If the integrity and authenticity has been verified successfully, the system has to continue with its regular start-up process. If the integrity and authenticity check has failed, however, the Machine.trustedPlatformExecutableLaunchBehavior offers a configuration option on how to proceed with the start-up process.

Failed authenticity checks ⌈ The Base Software shall select the trusted platform mode based on the value of Machine.trustedPlatformExecutableLaunchBehavior. ⌋

The configuration of the three modes is done via the trustedPlatformExecutableLaunchBehavior attribute within the Processed Manifests. The configuration option is only allowed to be processed after the integrity and authenticity of the relevant Processed Manifests has been verified.

These three modes of the Machine.trustedPlatformExecutableLaunchBehavior are:

  • monitorMode
  • noTrustedPlatformSupport
  • strictMode

Launch Behavior Validation ⌈ The Base Software shall stop the start-up sequence of the Adaptive Platform if the integrity or authenticity check of the Processed Manifests containing the trustedPlatformExecutableLaunchBehavior selection has failed and switch to the unrecoverable state. ⌋

……本章内容较长已节选，完整内容见「本地文件」中的纯文本全文。

docs.title: 20. Monitor 模式
docs.text:
原文标题：Monitor Mode

In monitorMode, the integrity and authenticity checks are performed, but the start-up process is not affected. Hence, the Adaptive Platform starts up even if the file system has been compromised.

Monitor Mode ⌈ In monitorMode, if a check (, , and ) fails then the Base Software shall log the failure as DltMessage FailedIntegrityOrAuthenticityCheck and continue regular startup of the Adaptive Platform. ⌋

monitorMode is useful when the integrator wants the system to keep running, even if the platform is not considered trusted. In this case, the integrator might use additional measures outside the scope of Adaptive AUTOSAR, like e.g. restricted key access when using an HSM that supports this feature.

monitorMode is also useful during development phase, when frequent changes on the Adaptive Platform are performed and keeping the authentication tag (e.g. signatures) valid is a tedious task.

docs.title: 21. Strict 模式
docs.text:
原文标题：Strict Mode

In strictMode, the Adaptive Platform ensures that no Processes are executed, where the integrity and authenticity of the corresponding Executables, manifests or linked library could not be verified.

Strict Mode - Execution manifest ⌈ In strictMode, the Base Software shall prevent the execution of an Executable if the integrity or authenticity check of the corresponding processed Execution Manifests has failed. ⌋

Strict Mode - Service Instance manifests ⌈ In strictMode, the Base Software shall prevent the execution of an Executable if the integrity or authenticity check of at least one of the corresponding processed Service Instance Manifests has failed. ⌋

Strict Mode - Executables ⌈ In strictMode, the Base Software shall allow to start a Process only if the integrity and authenticity of the corresponding Executable and all shared objects linked with it was successfully verified. ⌋

Executable code can be provided by executables and by statically linked shared objects linked by the executable. The Base Software cannot determine dynamically linked shared objects and thus these needs to be validated through an alternative, implementation specific, mechanism.

docs.title: 25. Default Values
docs.text:
This section defines default values for lower layer software (not related to an individual functional cluster) where useful for selected configuration parameters (where provision of such default value seems to be straightforward). These are defined in . The motivation for providing these values is to simplify setting up an adaptive development project.

In other words the default values are meant to guide certain roles (e.g. developer, integrator) which values to choose to quickly get to a working configuration for Adaptive Machines. This document lists default values for parameters, which were proposed by AUTOSAR partners, based on experience from development projects. By intention, it makes no distinction between design and deployment.

Some default values are taken over from . When there is no equivalent note provided, a default value is specified by AUTOSAR partners. It is worth noting that in any case the parameters and their default settings have been chosen for the optimization of in-vehicle communication between a AUTOSAR adaptive or classic platform instance with some vehicle local communication peer.

docs.text: Qualified attribute name Default Value Description MachineDesign.tcpIpIcmpProps.icmpV4Props.tcpIpIcmpV4EchoReplyEnabled FALSE enables or disables transmission of ICMPv4 messages. docs.title: 29. Default values for ICMPv6 parameters
docs.text:
Qualified attribute name Default Value Description MachineDesign.tcpIpIcmpProps.icmpV6Props.tcpIpIcmpV6EchoReplyAvoidFragmentation TRUE Defines whether the echo reply is only transmitted in case that the incoming ICMPv6 Echo Request (Pings) fits the MTU of the respective interface, i.e. can be transmitted without IPv6 fragmentation. Assumption is that fragmentation of ICMP echo request will be no issue inside vehicle network (based on Ethernet communication). MachineDesign.tcpIpIcmpProps.icmpV6Props.tcpIpIcmpV6EchoReplyEnabled TRUE Parameter enables or disables transmission of ICMP echo reply message in case of a ICMP echo reception. MachineDesign.tcpIpIcmpProps.icmpV6Props.tcpIpIcmpV6HopLimit 255 time-to-live in number of hops for outgoing ICMPv6 packets. This mechanism prevents undelivered ICMPv6 packets to be forwarded between nodes for an unspecified number of hops. MachineDesign.tcpIpIcmpProps.icmpV6Props.tcpIpIcmpV6MsgDestinationUnreachableEnabled TRUE Parameter enables or disables transmission of ICMP Destination Unreachable Messages.

docs.title: 30. Default values for ARP parameters
docs.text: Qualified attribute name Default Value Description MachineDesign.ethIpProps.arpProps.tcpIpArpNumGratuitousArpOnStartup 0 number of gratuitous ARP replies which shall be sent on assignment of a new IP address. This is a specific type of ARP response message which was not triggered by an ARP request message. MachineDesign.ethIpProps.arpProps.tcpIpArpPacketQueueEnabled FALSE Enables or disables support of the ARP packet queue according to IETF RFC 1122. Value is taken from classic platform . MachineDesign.ethIpProps.arpProps.tcpIpArpRequestTimeout 1 Timeout in seconds for the validity of ARP requests. After the transmission of an ARP request further transmission of ARP requests to the same destination shall be skipped for the specified duration. Value is taken from classic platform .

docs.title: 31. Default values for AutoIP parameters
docs.text: Qualified attribute name Default Value Description MachineDesign.ethIpProps.autoIpProps.tcpIpAutoIpInitTimeout 0 Specifies the time in seconds Auto-IP waits at startup, before beginning with ARP probing. This delay is used to give DHCP time to acquire a lease in case a DHCP server is present.

docs.title: 32. Default values for IPv4 fragmentation parameters
docs.text: Qualified attribute name Default Value Description MachineDesign.ethIpProps.fragmentationProps.tcpIpIpFragmentationRxEnabled FALSE Enables or disables support for reassembling of incoming datagrams that are fragmented according to IETF RFC 815 (IP Datagram ReassemblyAlgorithms). At least for in-vehicle communication with nodes connected to MTU of same size, Ethernet fragmentation is not needed. In case this argumentation is followed subsequent fragmentation related parameters, all of them taking the following prefix MachineDesign.ethIpProps.fragmentationProps. have no role in setting default values: tcpIpIpNumFragments tcpIpIpNumReassDgrams tcpIpIpReassTimeout

docs.title: 34. Default values for NDP parameters
docs.text:
Qualified attribute name Default Value Description MachineDesign.ethIpProps.ndpProps.tcpIpNdpDefaultReachableTime 120 reachable time for NDP in seconds as specified by IETF RFC 4861. MachineDesign.ethIpProps.ndpProps.tcpIpNdpDefaultRetransTimer in the range between 0.1 and 1 retransmission timer for NDP in seconds as specified by IETF RFC 4861. MachineDesign.ethIpProps.ndpProps.tcpIpNdpDefaultRouterListSize 2 size of router list. These entries may be used to send NDP messages. Value is taken from classic platform . MachineDesign.ethIpProps.ndpProps.tcpIpNdpDefensiveProcessing FALSE If enabled the NDP shall only process Neighbor Advertisements which are received in reaction to a previously transmitted Neighbor Solicitation as well as skipping updates to the Neighbor Cache based on received Neighbor Solicitations. If disabled all Neighbor Advertisements and Solicitations shall be processed as specified in RFC4861. docs.title: 文档简介
docs.text:
This specification describes the functionality, API and the configuration for the AUTOSAR Adaptive Diagnostic Management (DM).

The DM is a diagnostic server implementation that realizes

  • a UDS server instance according to ISO 14229-1

  • SOVD according to ASAM for the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform.

As transport layer for UDS, a flexible concept is applied. The DoIP protocol based on ISO 13400-2:2019, including ISO 13400-2:2019/Amd 1:2023 or a custom implementation of a transport protocol can be used.

For SOVD, the HTTP/HTTPS transport protocol with REST services is used.

docs.title: 模块依赖
docs.text: This chapter defines the dependencies of this functional cluster to other functional clusters. AUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between functional clusters to allow efficient implementations which might depend e.g., on the used operating system. The goal of this chapter is to provide an informative guideline for the interactions between functional clusters without specifying syntactical details. This ensures compatibility between documents specifying different functional clusters and supports parallel implementation of different functional clusters. Details of internal interfaces are up to the platform provider. Additional internal interfaces, parameters, and return values can be added. A detailed technical architecture documentation of the overall AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform is provided in .

docs.title: 1. 简介与功能概述
docs.text:
原文标题：Introduction and functional overview

This specification describes the functionality, API and the configuration for the AUTOSAR Adaptive Diagnostic Management (DM).

The DM is a diagnostic server implementation that realizes

  • a UDS server instance according to ISO 14229-1

  • SOVD according to ASAM for the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform.

As transport layer for UDS, a flexible concept is applied. The DoIP protocol based on ISO 13400-2:2019, including ISO 13400-2:2019/Amd 1:2023 or a custom implementation of a transport protocol can be used.

For SOVD, the HTTP/HTTPS transport protocol with REST services is used.
